# Intake Brief: Fair round-robin work scheduling with priority override (WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V)

## Problem Statement
The `dispatchFromCoordination` leader path in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` selects from the shared coordination file (`downtime-coordination.json`) by iterating entries in file order within each tier. With multiple projects contributing (ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine), this allows the same project to monopolise consecutive dispatch slots. We need globally-fair distribution with an exception for critical-priority items.

## Users

- **Agent — Automated downtime worker (primary):** As a downtime worker I want dispatches to fairly represent all contributing projects, so that no single project starves others of agent attention.
- **Developer / Project owner:** As a developer with work in an unserved project, I want the scheduler to eventually assign my project's candidate even when another project has more frequent offers, so that my backlog makes progress.

### User Stories
- As the downtime dispatcher leader, when entries exist from multiple projects at the same tier, I select the project whose last dispatch (in any tier) is oldest (round-robin), so that projects get a fair share of slots.
- As a project owner with a `critical`-priority offer on file, my next dispatch should bypass round-robin and run immediately (still at its stage-appropriate skill), so that urgent work is not delayed by fairness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `dispatchFromCoordination` selects across the shared coordination entries in **global cross-project round-robin** order: among equally-eligible (tier-matched, non-critical) entries, the project whose `worklogRoot` was least-recently dispatched (with persistence across leader restarts / cycles) is chosen first. New / unknown roots sort first (never penalised). A single persistent cursor/state per worklog root (e.g. in a JSON file alongside the coordination file) drives the ordering; concurrent leaders do not corrupt the cursor (fail-open).
- [ ] When **any** entry on file is a `critical`-priority open item at a dispatchable stage (`idea` / `intake_complete` / `plan_complete` within caps; stage-appropriate skill), the leader dispatches that critical entry **immediately** ahead of all non-critical entries, regardless of round-robin position. Within the critical subset, selection remains deterministic (existing priority/sortIndex tie-break — one item per project, so round-robin is not needed inside critical).
- [ ] The critical override is **global** (evaluated before any tier loop): a critical in `plan_complete` outranks a non-critical `audit`, and a critical `idea` outranks a non-critical `implement`, matching the intent "jump to the front of the queue". The existing freeze (audit/implement skipped while frozen) and caps (`risk <= Medium && effort <= Medium` for `plan_complete`, including critical) are retained.
- [ ] After a successful dispatch (or a `spawn-failed`/`marker-write-failed` claim that still consumes the entry), the round-robin cursor/state advances to mark that project's `worklogRoot` as most-recently served, so the next dispatch in **any** tier starts from the following project.
- [ ] Existing `downtime-worker` and `coordination` tests still pass, plus new tests prove: (a) with two non-critical entries from different projects at the same tier, consecutive dispatches alternate projects; (b) a newly-arrived critical from project B is dispatched next even though round-robin would choose project A; (c) cursor persists across a simulated leader restart.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Must build on the existing coordination machinery (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` lock + atomic write, `machine-coordination.ts` single machine dir) — no new daemon or external dependency.
- Fail-open on missing/corrupt round-robin state (behaves as if no history — original file order), never throws or starves dispatch.
- No behaviour change to `wl next` / single-project flows; this is strictly the multi-project leader path (`coordinationDir` present).
- Preserve dispatched-marker exclusion and CAS claim ordering already in `dispatchFromCoordination`.
- Each project currently registers at most one offer per cycle, so per-project multiplicity can be treated as one entry per root — design should not break if that grows, but need not optimise for many-per-root.

## Existing State
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination` groups fetched entries by tier (`audit` → `critical` → `implement` → `plan` → `intake`) and iterates each group in file order (`entries` array order). No cross-project fairness: repeated offers from the same root can win every slot when they re-queue quickly.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` provides a per-tier persistent cursor for the *legacy* `selectWithRotation` path (unused in coordination mode); the new requirement is **global, cross-tier** round-robin across `worklogRoot`s.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` manages `downtime-coordination.json` with atomic tmp+rename and an `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock` / `withCoordLock`), and already carries `worklogRoot` per entry; `machine-coordination.ts` makes the file machine-wide.
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-cross-root.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.test.ts`.
- Contributing projects: ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine (each instance writes one entry via `runCoordinationCheckIn`).

## Desired Change
- Introduce a **global per-project round-robin** ordering for `dispatchFromCoordination`: track last-dispatched `worklogRoot` (persistent JSON alongside the coordination file, e.g. `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`), sort same-tier eligible candidates by "least-recently-served first" before dispatch, and advance the cursor on each consumed entry.
- Promote the **critical override** to a global pre-tier check: re-fetch → if any dispatchable critical exists, dispatch the first critical immediately (respecting freeze/caps), before the tier-ordered round-robin loop.
- Add/extend tests to cover alternating-project fairness, critical jump-ahead, and cursor durability; update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and relevant code comments.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Needs updated `dispatchFromCoordination` + new helpers for global round-robin ordering / cursor advance
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — May gain small helpers or remain unchanged (new state file is separate)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` — May be reused/extended or a new `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` added for worklogRoot-keyed persistence
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — Reference for machine-dir resolution used by the new state file
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Needs new fair-scheduling test cases
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Needs updated dispatch ordering description (fair scheduling + critical override)

## Related Work
- Parent area: `WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL` (Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election + shared coordination file), `WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN` (Single machine-wide leader), `WL-0MTII45EP002DWK6` (Cross-directory tier dispatch)
- Preceding round-robin work: `WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6` + `downtime-round-robin.ts` / `downtime-round-robin.test.ts` (per-tier cursor, now superseded by global root-level rotation)
- Tier / dispatch reference: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:COORDINATION_TIER_ORDER`, `classifyItemForDispatch`, `COORDINATION_FILE` / `readCoordinationFile` in `coordination.ts`
- Follow-up opportunity: if per-root multiplicity grows beyond one, consider weighted or deficit round-robin (record as a linked work item, not in scope)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** Cursor file races between leaders → Mitigation: reuse the existing `withCoordLock` / tmp+rename pattern; fail-open when lock is contended.
- **Risk:** New critical items arriving between fetch and dispatch could be missed → Mitigation: critical check happens on the same single fetch pass; subsequent arrivals wait one cycle (acceptable at 30-min check-in cadence).
- **Risk:** Stale-entry pruning removes a root before its round-robin turn → Mitigation: pruned roots drop from ordering automatically; no ghost cursor entries block others.
- **Risk:** Scope creep (e.g. per-entry priority weighting beyond critical) → Mitigation: explicitly out of scope; non-critical priorities are treated as equally round-robined (per operator: one item per project).
- **Assumption:** At most one entry per `worklogRoot` per cycle — holds today; ordering by `worklogRoot` last-served is equivalent to ordering by entry last-served.
- **Assumption:** "Jump to the front" means dispatch before any non-critical regardless of tier, not just within the same tier — confirmed with operator (clarification round: globally, dispatch immediately).
- **Assumption:** Persistence should survive leader restarts and machine reboot → file on disk in the machine coordination dir, not in-memory only.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What constitutes a 'project' for fair scheduling?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project downtime scheduling recently implemented — leader election with one work item per project via the herdr extension. Currently ContextHub, ../SorraAgents, ../AI_Hell, ../Tableau-Card-Engine." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Is this about `wl next` or the coordination dispatch?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project case — nothing to do with `wl next`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "When a project has a critical item, does it jump the queue?" — Answer (user): "yes" (affirmative — critical from any project jumps ahead). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Do non-critical priorities (high/medium/low) matter within round-robin?" — Answer (user): "I believe each project only registers a single work item so this is not important." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Round-robin scope — per-tier or globally?" — Answer (user): "globally" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Critical override granularity — immediate dispatch or just cursor bump?" — Answer (user): "dispatch immediately" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Should the cursor persist across cycles/restarts?" — Answer (user): "persistent" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.

# Dispatch-logs Skill: Generate Global Dispatch Reports

A `/skill:dispatch-logs` command that produces a concise, human-readable (or JSON) 24-hour dispatch activity report across all projects on the machine — including leader state, timeline, errors, and coordination status — with support for custom time windows and per-project filtering.

## Problem Statement

Operators investigating overnight dispatches must manually aggregate `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` files across all projects on the machine. There is no single command to produce a concise 24-hour (or custom window) global dispatch report.

## Users

- **Operator on-call**: Needs a quick view of what dispatches ran overnight and whether any errors occurred.
- **Debugging engineer**: Tracing a specific dispatch failure across projects.
- **Team lead**: Reviewing dispatch activity trends over a custom time window.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:dispatch-logs` produces a human-readable report covering all projects on the machine for the last 24 hours (default window).
2. All invocation flags work correctly: `--hours N`, `--since`/`--until` ISO timestamps, `--project <name>`, and `--json` for machine-readable output.
3. The report includes five sections: (a) leader summary, (b) dispatch timeline, (c) error summary, (d) coordination state, and (e) known issues.
4. Gracefully handles the case when no dispatch logs exist (produces an empty/clean report, not an error).
5. Unit tests pass for log parsing, argument handling, and report structure (using mocked log files).
6. SKILL.md is complete with name, description, invocation examples, and frontmatter.

## Constraints

- Log files are in JSONL format (one JSON object per line).
- Machine coordination state lives in `~/.herdr/downtime/` (two JSON files).
- Must skip `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` directories during project root discovery.
- Default window is 24 hours from `Date.now()`; custom windows use ISO 8601 timestamps.

## Existing State

- Per-worklog dispatch logs exist at `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- Machine-wide coordination at `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` and `downtime-leader-lease.json`.
- Companion debug item (WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV) adds per-strike stderr/exitCode — the dispatch-logs skill should note when this data is unavailable.

## Desired Change

Create a new skill in `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/` with:
- `SKILL.md` — skill definition with frontmatter and invocation docs.
- `scripts/dispatch-logs.py` — Python script implementing the report generation.
- `tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — unit tests with mocked data.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/SKILL.md` — New skill definition file.
- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/scripts/dispatch-logs.py` — Core logic: argument parsing, log discovery, parsing, report generation.
- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — Unit tests.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` — Read-only coordination state.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-leader-lease.json` — Read-only leader lease.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: Resist adding extra report sections beyond the five specified (leader summary, dispatch timeline, error summary, coordination state, known issues).
- **Discovery performance**: Walking from `~` to find all project roots could be slow on machines with many repositories; consider caching or a configurable root list.
- **JSONL format consistency**: Assumes all projects write logs in the same JSONL format; malformed lines should be skipped gracefully.
- **Coordination files**: Assumes `~/.herdr/downtime/` files are present and readable; handle missing files gracefully.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV** — "Downtime dispatcher: make wl-error pauses debuggable" (companion; provides richer per-strike data the dispatch-logs skill should report on).
- **WL-0MU4URK4H006OFCE** — "Extend dispatch log schema and add pane lifecycle monitor" (may affect log parsing).
- **WL-0MU8808ZY0091JIA** — "Downtime dispatcher: log the actual no-dispatch reason" (enriches available log data).
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — "Log herdr downtime dispatches" (established the per-worklog log architecture).

# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.
- **Shared scoring:** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`computeScore`/`reSort`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`) and `src/commands/next.ts` auto `reSort` — shared by `wl next` but not required to change for this contract; the observable contract is Herdr list head.
- All divergence gaps mapped in WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q (cap 32 / mandatory merge / stage-scoped calls / audit `wl list` source / tier order / risk-effort gates / code-freeze tri-state, etc.) — eliminated by consuming the Herdr order directly.

## Desired change

Replace the dispatcher's independent tier ordering with consumption of the Herdr selection list head:

- Refactor `downtime-worker.ts` to invoke (or share code with) the Herdr fetcher/selection pipeline to obtain the ordered candidate sequence, then apply only the necessary safety filters (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight/active-audit) sequentially on that sequence.
- Remove or dead-code the tier-ordering / per-stage `wl next` / audit `wl list` ranking path from the dispatch decision (or leave only as unused fallback behind a feature flag with a clear deprecation note).
- Document the contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; filters, not ranking") in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Herdr selection pipeline reused by dispatcher
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always + browseItemCount logic
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — regroupWorkItems / assignItemGroups ordering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatchDowntimeWork to be refactored to consume list head (+ fixtures)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — computeScore/reSort/filterCandidates as used by fetcher (not dispatcher ranking)
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — wl next entry point as used by fetcher
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher contract doc
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr list contract doc

## Related work

- Investigation: WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q — downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (producer determination revised 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, superseding WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) → follow-up direction is this item.
- WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (symptom of cap/mandatory interaction; not blocking but shares fetcher context)
- WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — Herdr smart selection / in_review / root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG — implement tier + risk/effort filters wired into wl next / dispatcher (removed or converted to filters in this work)
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging (preserved as filters)
- WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (cursor handling to reconcile with Herdr order)
- RCA docs: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — prior tier/re-dispatch incidents

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts` (including coordination leader path if any).
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" — confirmed 2026-09-02 (Herdr list canonical; dispatcher consumes head).
- Risk: code-freeze / audit safety behavior at head — if the list head must be skipped, the skip order must be explicit and remain a filter on the Herdr sequence; document clearly.
- Risk: `in_review` mandatory-always items in the list — dispatcher taking the head must still respect `completed`/`in_review` dispatchability; filter vs ranking distinction must be explicit to avoid re-dispatching audits.
- Risk: spare-capacity / idle-budget / round-robin cursor logic must be reconciled as filters or removed; otherwise a second ordering re-emerges.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches herdr selection and downtime-worker — keep scope to dispatcher-consumes-head; do not rework scoring or grouping unless required for the contract. Extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the Herdr list order or the dispatcher tier order?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, rescoping WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2; supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS): **Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Dispatcher selects the first item in that list — no second ranking. Source: producer comment WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first)?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **Unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`". Source: same producer determination.
- Q3: "For sampling, which `browseItemCount` / `wl next -n` window and which worklog root should be the reference?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS as affirmed by WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **LGTM** — default `browseItemCount` / ContextHub root / `wl next -n 20` accepted as sampling reference. Source: producer comment on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.

No open questions. Interview skipped — seed context and revised producer determination (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1) already provide a clear, testable brief.

# Intake Brief — Add a priority icon to the selection list (WL-0MTQYTA20009YXBT)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist selection list shows status, stage, producer review, and epic icons in its icon prefix, but the priority icon is only rendered as text after the title. Users scanning the list should see a priority icon alongside the other status indicators for at-a-glance prioritisation.

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using the Herdr worklist to browse and triage work items.
  - User story: "As a developer scanning the Herdr worklist, I want to see a priority icon as the first icon in each row so I can quickly identify urgent items without reading the full priority text."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Herdr worklist selection list icon prefix (in `getIconPrefix` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) includes a priority icon as the first icon, before the existing agent status slot.
2. The priority icon uses the existing `PRIORITY_ICONS` map from `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`: critical → 🚨, high → ⭐, medium → 📋, low → 🐢.
3. The priority icon respects the existing `noIcons` option — when icons are disabled, `PRIORITY_FALLBACK` text is shown instead.
4. The `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH` is increased to accommodate the additional icon (from 12 to 13 cells), and alignment is preserved.
5. The work item `priority` field is already passed through the item type accepted by `getIconPrefix`.
6. All existing tests continue to pass; new tests are added for the priority icon in the prefix (emoji, fallback, null/undefined priority, noIcons mode).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.

## Constraints

- Must extend the existing `getIconPrefix` function in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — do not create a parallel icon system.
- Must preserve the existing `WL_NO_ICONS=1` / `noIcons` option behaviour.
- Must not break the fixed-width alignment (`ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`) — adjust the constant if needed.
- Visual-only change in the Herdr worklist rendering; no persisted data model changes.
- The priority icon must appear **first** in the icon prefix row.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`**: The `getIconPrefix` function composes an icon prefix with columns: agent status (fixed-width slot), status icon, stage/audit icon, producer review flag, and optional epic icon. The `PRIORITY_ICONS` and `PRIORITY_FALLBACK` maps exist but are not used in the prefix.
- **`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`**: Calls `getIconPrefix(item, { noIcons })` and prepends the result before the item ID/title. The `item` type already includes `priority?: string`.
- **Priority text** is already rendered after the title as `${priorityIcon(item.priority, { noIcons })} ${item.priority}` (line 1255 of worklist.ts).

## Desired change

1. **`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`**:
   - Update `getIconPrefix` to prepend the priority icon as the first icon in the prefix.
   - The new column layout (left to right):
     - 0. Priority icon
     - 1. Agent status (existing fixed-width slot)
     - 2. Status icon
     - 3. Stage icon (for in_review items, shows audit-aware icon instead)
     - 4. Producer review flag
     - 5. Optional epic icon
   - Update `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH` from 12 to 13 to account for the additional icon.
   - Update the JSDoc comment for `getIconPrefix` to document the new column layout.

2. **Tests**: Add/update tests for the priority icon in `getIconPrefix` (emoji, fallback, null/undefined priority, noIcons mode).

3. **Documentation**: Update any relevant documentation (e.g., `docs/icons-design.md` if it exists).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — Update `getIconPrefix` to prepend priority icon; update `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — No changes needed (item type already includes `priority`)
- `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` — New tests for priority icon in `getIconPrefix`

# Intake Brief — Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace (route each prefix to its own tab) (WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC)

**Headline**: Extend the now-correct Dispatcher-workspace anchor so every automated downtime dispatch lands in a per-project tab inside the Dispatcher workspace, named after the work-item prefix (e.g. `WL`, `TCE`), giving operators instant per-project separation without leaving the neutral workspace.

## Problem statement

The automated downtime dispatcher has been fixed to always spawn into a dedicated **Dispatcher** workspace regardless of which herdr instance holds the leader lease (WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG / WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX, F1–F3 landed on `origin/dev`). All dispatches currently share the single root tab/pane in that workspace. With two active worklogs (ContextHub `WL-…`, Tableau Card Engine `CG-/TCE-…`, plus other roots) this collapses per-project separation — overnight runs for different projects intermix in one grid and operators must inspect each pane's `cwd`/label to tell them apart.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running 2+ project workspaces** (e.g. ContextHub, Podcast-editor, Tableau Card Engine):
  > "As an operator, I want every automated downtime pane that belongs to project prefix `TCE` to appear in a `TCE` tab of the Dispatcher workspace (and `WL` panes in a `WL` tab), so I can see per-project progress at a glance without mixing projects in one grid."

- **On-call / overnight dispatch reviewer**:
  > "As an on-call engineer reviewing morning dispatches, I want the Dispatcher workspace to contain one tab per project (labelled by the work-item prefix), so I can sweep each project's automated work independently."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-prefix tab routing inside the Dispatcher workspace** — an automated downtime dispatch for work item `<PREFIX>-<hash>` creates (if absent) or reuses a tab labelled `<PREFIX>` inside the machine-wide Dispatcher workspace and spawns its pane inside that tab. Example: `WL-0MTO…` → `WL` tab, `TCE-…` / `CG-…` → tab named exactly after the id prefix before `-` (so `TCE` items land in `TCE`, `WL` items in `WL`). Verified via `herdr tab list` (tabs filtered to `workspace_id == Dispatcher` carry `label == prefix`) and `herdr pane list` (each `Downtime triggered …` pane's `workspace_id == Dispatcher` and `tab_id` equals the prefix tab's `tab_id`, with `cwd` equal to the item's worklog root).
2. **Idempotent, concurrent-safe tab provisioning** — the first dispatch for a previously unseen prefix creates the tab exactly once; concurrent first-dispatches for the same new prefix do not create duplicate tabs with the same label in the Dispatcher workspace. Re-provisioning handles stale state: a persisted per-prefix anchor whose tab/pane is no longer alive is detected and re-created on the next dispatch for that prefix.
3. **No regression to existing dispatcher invariants** — Dispatcher-workspace anchoring (no fallback to the leader's current pane — `anchor-unavailable` still means "no dispatch this cycle"), per-item `cwd` forwarding, CAS `wl update --if-status/--if-stage` claim, staged-marker exclusion, `code-freeze` and `needsProducerReview` gates, selection/coordination/round-robin semantics, and dispatch audit logs (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) remain unchanged; pane spawn still goes through `send-to-pi.sh` / `grid.py` (now targeting the per-prefix tab's anchor pane rather than the single workspace anchor when a prefix tab exists).
4. **No leftover duplicate workspace or orphan tab state** — after the change there remains exactly one `Dispatcher` workspace (label `Dispatcher`, `w13` today) holding all per-prefix tabs; repeated dispatches for the same prefix do not leak extra tabs or panes beyond the expected grid growth; a persisted file (e.g. extended `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` or a new `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` in the machine coordination dir) tracks `{ workspaceId, byPrefix: { "<PREFIX>": { tabId, paneId } } }` under the coordination lock and is the authority for reuse.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Automated downtime dispatch only — scope is `dispatchFromCoordination` / `dispatchDowntimeWork` → `dispatchClaimedTier`; manual `open-worklist` / `open-pi-agent` flows keep their current-pane/tab behavior.
- Single `Dispatcher` workspace (C0) is retained — per-project separation is by **tabs** inside it, not by additional workspaces.
- Prefix extraction is the work-item id substring before the first `-` (e.g. `WL-…` → `WL`, `TCE-…` → `TCE`, `CG-…` → `CG`); tab label is exactly that prefix (case-preserved, no normalisation beyond the raw prefix).
- Tab/pane provisioning must use the existing machine coordination dir (`~/.herdr/downtime`, via `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts`) and the coordination lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock`) — no new lock mechanism; `herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <PREFIX> --no-focus` (or `workspace create` + `tab create`) and `herdr pane split --pane <anchorPaneId>` / `grid.py` remain the herdr surface.
- Fail-safe: if the per-prefix tab/anchor cannot be resolved/provisioned, the dispatch degrades to `anchor-unavailable` (no dispatch this cycle), never to a leader-workspace fallback or to the wrong tab.
- Herdr CLI JSON shapes may vary across versions (`tab_id` vs `tabId`, `pane_id` vs `paneId`, nested `result`) — parsers must tolerate variants and log raw output on parse failure rather than silently producing `anchor-unavailable` every cycle.

## Existing state

- **C0 anchor-by-ID landed on `origin/dev` (WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG):** `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` provisions one `Dispatcher` workspace + root pane and persists `{ paneId, workspaceId }` to `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` under the coordination lock with an aliveness (`pane get`) check and stale re-provision; `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchClaimedTier` resolves `getDispatcherAnchor(cwd)` before the CAS claim and forwards `anchorId` to `spawnAgentPane` → `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` → `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py --cwd <target>` (split + rebalance around the anchor) or plain `pane split --pane <id>`.
- **Live state:** `herdr workspace list` shows one authoritative `Dispatcher` workspace `w13:t1` (pane_count 1); `herdr tab list` shows `w13:t1` label `1`; `herdr pane list` shows `w13:p2` `Downtime triggered audit …` (evidence the anchor path is working after the WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX fix).
- **Gap:** all prefixes currently share `w13:t1`; there is no `herdr tab create --label <PREFIX>` path, no per-prefix persistence, and `grid.py` / `send-to-pi.sh` have no tab-aware anchoring — a new prefix-aware resolver plus `tab create` + per-prefix anchor mapping is required.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the Dispatcher anchor module to per-prefix tabs** — replace/augment the single-anchor persistence with a map `byPrefix` (e.g. `{ workspaceId, byPrefix: { "WL": { tabId, paneId }, "TCE": { tabId, paneId } } }`) stored in the machine coordination dir; the resolver `getDispatcherTabAnchor(cwd, prefix)` (or `getDispatcherAnchor` extended to take a prefix) does: ensure the `Dispatcher` workspace exists → list tabs in that workspace (`herdr tab list --workspace <id>`) to find `label == prefix` → validate the tab's anchor pane is alive (`pane get`) → return `{ workspaceId, tabId, paneId }` or, if absent/stale, create it under the coordination lock (`herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <PREFIX> --no-focus`, capture `tab_id` + `root_pane.pane_id`), persist under lock, and return it. Double-check inside the lock before creating to avoid duplicates.
2. **Wire the per-prefix anchor into the dispatch path** — `dispatchClaimedTier` derives the prefix from `candidate.id.split("-")[0]` after selection and resolves the per-prefix anchor **before** the CAS claim; the resolved `paneId` (tab's anchor pane) is forwarded as `anchorId` to `spawnAgentPane` exactly as today so `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` and `grid.py --cwd <target>` grow the correct tab's grid. The legacy `DispatcherAnchor` type remains for the workspace-level fallback if needed, but the primary path is per-prefix.
3. **Idempotency & failure modes** — concurrent tab creates for the same prefix serialize on the coordination lock and double-check inside the lock; missing/ambiguous herdr output fails closed to `anchor-unavailable` with a diagnostic log line (`[worklog-plugin] Dispatcher tab anchor …`) rather than a silent fallback; stale panes trigger re-provisioning on next dispatch for that prefix.
4. **Tests + docs** — add unit/integration coverage for: first-dispatch-for-prefix creates labelled tab and persists mapping; second dispatch reuses the tab; concurrent first-dispatches do not duplicate; stale pane re-creates; malformed `tab create` output is handled; dispatch still forwards correct `cwd` and audit logs unchanged. Update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (per-prefix tab invariant, troubleshooting "pane landed in wrong tab/workspace") and code comments around the anchor resolver.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — Dispatcher workspace + new per-prefix tab anchor provisioning, persistence (machine dir), aliveness check, lock-guarded create-or-reuse.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchClaimedTier` / `dispatchFromCoordination` / `buildDowntimePaneArgs`; prefix extraction, per-prefix anchor resolution before claim, `anchorId` forwarding.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` / `defaultDispatcherAnchorResolver` wiring; production injection of the per-prefix resolver.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — `--anchor <paneId>` handling; must split the per-prefix tab's anchor pane (never `pane current` in anchor mode); `--cwd <target>` forwarding unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` — Grid rebalance around the per-prefix tab's anchor pane.
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — `getMachineCoordinationDir` / `ensureMachineCoordinationDir`; machine dir resolution for the tab-anchor file(s).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — `tryAcquireCoordLock`; concurrency guard for tab provisioning.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` (and/or new `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`) — Persisted per-prefix tab/pane map (currently single-anchor shape; will be extended).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Dispatcher anchor + new per-prefix tab invariant and troubleshooting.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — Existing anchor tests (extend for tab cases).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — Dispatcher wiring tests (cover per-prefix `anchorId` forwarding).

## Related work

- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG** — Parent epic "Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace regardless of project (C0: anchor-by-ID into dedicated Dispatcher workspace)" (children F1–F3 completed: `WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U`, `WL-0MTR2HLLJ009PTPJ`, `WL-0MTR2JOTE006T3XT`; commits `893d6d22`, `69ae52f2`, `c7620f17` on `origin/dev`).
- **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX** — Follow-up fix "Downtime dispatches land in Podcast workspace instead of Dispatcher workspace" (critical, implements anchor persistence / routing repair; doc already notes `w13` as authoritative Dispatcher).
- **C1 (this item)** — originally deferred in WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX constraints as "Single neutral Dispatcher workspace — not per-project tabs (deferred to follow-up C1)". This work item IS that C1.
- **WL-0MSGAEXER000707R** — Prior `target_cwd` / `--cwd` forwarding fix touching the same `send-to-pi.sh` / `grid.py` path.
- File matches: `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: herdr CLI output shape drift for `tab create` / `tab list`** — new parsers for `tab create --workspace` (keys `tab_id`/`tabId`/`id`, nested `result.tab` / `result.root_pane`) may break across herdr versions, causing every per-prefix dispatch to degrade to `anchor-unavailable`. **Mitigation:** broaden key fallbacks, log raw output on parse failure, add a unit test that asserts against the live CLI shape; reuse the existing `workspace create` parsing pattern from `dispatcher-anchor.ts:createWorkspace`.
- **Risk: duplicate tabs on concurrent first-dispatch for same new prefix** — without a lock-guarded double-check, two leaders could both see "no tab for TCE" and create two `TCE` tabs. **Mitigation:** provision under `tryAcquireCoordLock`; double-check `tab list` inside the lock before `tab create`; treat existing label as success even if `tab create` races.
- **Risk: stale per-prefix anchor (tab closed, pane dead) goes undetected** — a deleted tab's persisted `paneId` would make every dispatch for that prefix fail closed until re-provisioned. **Mitigation:** aliveness check (`pane get` + `tab get` or `tab list` filter) before reuse; on failure fall through to re-provision under lock.
- **Risk: tab label collisions / case sensitivity** — prefix `wl` vs `WL` could create two tabs or clobber. **Mitigation:** tab label is exactly the raw prefix as extracted (case-preserved); document as such — prefixes in this repo are uppercase (`WL`, `TCE`/`CG`) so no collision in practice.
- **Risk: scope creep into multi-workspace or archive UX** — hour-bucket archive (C2), auto-close sweeps, or workspace-per-project could re-enter scope. **Mitigation:** strictly C1 as defined: one `Dispatcher` workspace, one tab per prefix, no additional workspace or non-downtime tab behaviour.
- **Assumption:** `herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <PREFIX> --no-focus` exists and creates a tab in the given workspace without stealing focus, returning `tab_id` + `root_pane.pane_id` (herdr 0.7.x CLI as observed for `workspace create`).
- **Assumption:** `herdr pane split --pane <id>` works from a pane in a non-focused tab/workspace without stealing focus (prior C0 verification assumption, still holds for per-prefix tab anchor panes).
- **Assumption:** The work-item id prefix before the first `-` is the desired tab label (as requested: "Name the tab after the work item prefix, e.g. TCE and WL"); if the TCE project historically used `CG-…`, the resulting tab will be `CG` — acceptable unless the project migrates ids to `TCE-…`, in which case that prefix naturally produces a `TCE` tab.
- **Assumption:** The machine coordination dir `~/.herdr/downtime` (or `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` override) is writable by the leader and survives across herdr restarts so the per-prefix map persists.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Were the two misplaced dispatches that motivated the Dispatcher workspace automated downtime dispatches?" — Answer (user, prior intake WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX): **Yes, automated downtime dispatches**. Source: interactive reply in that intake.
- Q: "Should all downtime dispatches be forced into the Dispatcher workspace, or only automated ones?" — Answer (user, prior intake): **Just automated; manual `open-worklist`/`open-pi-agent` keep current-pane behaviour**. Carried forward here: per-prefix tabs apply only to automated downtime dispatch.
- Q: "What should the per-project tabs be named?" — Answer (user, this request): **After the work-item prefix, e.g. `TCE` for Tablea Card Engine and `WL` for ContextHub**. Source: `/intake` freeform arguments for WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC — "So Tablea Card Engine work items will be sent to one tab and ContextHub items will go to another. Name the tab after the work item prefix, e.g. TCE and WL". Final: implemented as `candidate.id.split("-",1)[0]` → tab label.
- Q: "Should a new prefix create a new tab automatically, or should tabs be pre-provisioned?" — Answer (agent inference, no producer input needed): **Auto-create on first dispatch for that prefix** — matches the existing on-demand `Dispatcher` workspace provisioning and requires no manual setup. Kept conservative; producer can review during planning if pre-provisioning is preferred.
- Q: "What happens if the TCE project's work items use prefix `CG` rather than `TCE`?" — Answer (agent inference): **Tab will be `CG`** (raw prefix), which still gives per-project separation for that worklog root. If the project migrates to `TCE-…` ids, that naturally routes to a `TCE` tab. Recorded as an assumption; flagged for producer confirmation at review.

## Related work (automated report)

*Populated by `/skill:find-related` in §7 — see work-item comments for the full report.*

# Intake Brief — Text inputs miss keypresses when extension is syncing — pause sync while user is typing (WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH)

## Problem statement

All in-extension screens that present a text input intermittently drop keypresses. The suspected cause is a background `wl sync` (and its follow-up list refresh/re-render) firing while the user is typing, contending for the TUI event loop or replacing render state mid-keystroke. There is no user value in syncing/refreshing while a form is active — it should be deferred until typing finishes.

## Users

- **Extension users typing in any form** — creators/editors filling fields in the Herdr worklist pane and any other in-extension overlay that accepts free-text input.
- **Operators triaging during incident flows** — users who rapidly fill forms while background workers run.

Example user stories:
- As a user filling the command-parameter form (`FormState` — unknown `<identifier>` prompts), I want every keystroke to register so I can submit the command without retyping.
- As a user writing a ship-it note / md note in the Ship-It dialog, I want the dialog to not lose characters when a periodic sync fires.
- As a user, I want the worklist to resume auto-sync/refresh promptly after I close the form, so I still see fresh data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Sync suppressed while typing:** While any text-input overlay is open, background `wl sync` is not spawned. Verified by running with `autoSync=true` and holding a form open for ≥2× `syncIntervalMs`: zero `wl sync` spawns (or, equivalently, the sync scheduler tick is skipped) — heartbeat/single-flight/visibility gates remain intact when not typing.
- [ ] **AC2 — Refresh/re-render suppressed while typing:** While any text-input overlay is open, auto-refresh list refetch/re-render is skipped so keypresses are not dropped. Verified by a deterministic unit/integration test that simulates rapid keystrokes into `FormState`/`ShipItDialogState` across a scheduled refresh tick — zero dropped characters; refresh resumes within one interval after the overlay closes.
- [ ] **AC3 — Coverage of all text-input screens:** The guard applies to every current text-input entry point (`form-dialog.ts` `FormState`, `ship-it-dialog.ts` `ShipItDialogState`, `md-note-edit.ts` note editing, and any other modal input) via a single shared predicate (e.g. `isTyping()` / `isInputActive()`) — not a per-screen copy-paste — so future inputs are covered by extending one place.
- [ ] **AC4 — No regression when not typing:** When no input is active, existing behaviour is unchanged: auto-refresh (30s default), auto-sync (60s default), visibility/heartbeat/DB-change gates, and downtime/mode-switch workers continue as before. Existing unit tests for `worklist.ts` / `auto-sync.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing & validation:** New unit tests cover: (a) sync tick skipped while form/ship-it dialog open; (b) refresh tick skipped while form/ship-it dialog open; (c) ticks resume after close; (d) typing simulation loses no keystrokes across ticks. A manual verification checklist is documented in a work-item comment (hold form open, observe no sync/refresh; close, observe resume).
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not regress existing gating: visibility (pause-when-hidden), single-flight, cross-instance heartbeat dedup, and DB-change skip must remain.
- Fix must be low-risk and narrowly scoped — gate the scheduler ticks, don't restructure the TUI event loop or form handling.
- Fire-and-forget sync semantics stay: skipping a tick is silent; no error surfacing while typing.
- Critical priority — dropped input is a data-loss-adjacent UX failure; prefer a minimal, reviewable patch.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` registers two periodic scheduler tasks: `refresh` (`autoRefresh`, 30s) and `sync` (`autoSync`, 60s, `fireImmediately:true`) which calls `doSync(true, heartbeatTtlMs)` then `doRefresh(false)`. Both are visibility-gated (`paneGate.visible()`) but have no typing/input gate, so they fire even while `formState !== null` / `shipItDialog !== null`.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` provides `runSync` / `SyncTimer` with `ifIdle` single-flight and heartbeat dedup, but no caller-side typing guard.
- Text-input overlays: `form-dialog.ts` (`FormState.handleInput`/`render`), `ship-it-dialog.ts` (`ShipItDialogState`), `md-note-edit.ts` (note edit flow that opens a `FormState`). Keypress handling in `worklist.ts` correctly routes to `formState.handleInput` when open, but the background tick still runs concurrently.
- Related hardening exists: thrash prevention / lock-storm fixes (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E), idle-gated refresh (WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I), pause-when-hidden (WL-0MSB447GC0004CAW). None gate on typing.

## Desired change

- Introduce a single shared predicate (e.g. `isInputActive()` / `isTyping()`) that is true whenever any text-input overlay is open (`formState !== null || shipItDialog !== null || md-note-edit active || filter text input if applicable`), and check it at the top of the `refresh` and `sync` scheduler tick handlers (alongside the existing `paneGate.visible()` check) to skip `doSync`/`doRefresh` while typing. Record the decision to resume on close (next tick fires normally — no extra immediate refresh required, or document if one is desired).
- Ensure the guard also covers any other periodic background refresh that would cause a re-render/lost focus while typing (audit explicitly whether `downtimeWorker`/`modeSwitchWorker` need gating; if not, document why — they don't touch the list render path while a modal is open).
- Add unit tests for the typed-gating and a manual smoke checklist; update in-code comments and docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add typing/input gate to scheduler tasks (`refresh` and `sync` ticks) and define shared `isInputActive` predicate.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — No direct change expected, but verify `runSync` single-flight/heartbeat semantics are preserved; add comment if gating is caller-side.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — Defines `FormState`; reference for predicate coverage.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog.ts` — Defines `ShipItDialogState`; reference for predicate coverage.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-note-edit.ts` — Note-edit text input flow; ensure covered.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Add typing-gated scheduler tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` — Regression guard (no behaviour change when not typing).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Documents the typing gate (pause background work while a form is open).
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — Typing-gate behaviour + manual smoke verification procedure.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E — wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync (completed) — prior sync thrash hardening.
- WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I / WL-0MSB445BP0057ZQT — idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget (completed) — existing gating to extend.
- WL-0MSB447GC0004CAW — Docs & verification: pause-when-hidden behavior (completed) — visibility gate sibling.
- WL-0MSBVBXEA0011OWF — Selection list refreshes immediately when its tab/pane regains focus (completed) — refresh cadence context.
- WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N — Pi extension polls even when selection list is not visible (completed) — similar "don't poll when not useful" pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Which screens count as "all in-extension screens that have text input"? — Answer (operator spec, WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH): All Herdr worklist pane overlays that accept free-text keystrokes via `FormState` / `ShipItDialogState` / `md-note-edit` (and any future text-input modal). Source: initial report "All in-extension screens that all text input will sometimes miss keypresses." No separate screen inventory was provided; brief assumes the three known overlays and a shared predicate to future-proof.
- Q: What exactly should be paused — `wl sync` only, or also list refresh / similar background work? — Answer (operator spec, WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH): "There is no need to do that (or similar) when the user is typing into a form in the extension." Interpreted as: at minimum suppress `wl sync` and the list `doRefresh` that would re-render/lose focus; audit other periodic ticks (downtime/mode-switch) and explicitly gate or document why not. Source: initial report sentence 2.
- Q: Should we debounce, buffer, or queue a refresh after typing ends? — Answer (Map, assumption — no producer input yet): Defer, don't queue: skip ticks while typing; next regular tick after close fires normally. If product wants an immediate post-close refresh, it can be added as a follow-up without changing the gating contract. Documented as assumption in Constraints/Desired change.

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (sibling timestamp symptom)
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF, WL-0MOYD0UAC003YJA3, WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW (auto re-sort features)

# Intake Brief — Smart Audit Re-instatement

**Headline:** When the audit freshness check (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) flags an audit as stale, the system should automatically review the changes made since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or flag the item for re-audit — rather than treating all post-audit changes as requiring a full re-run.

## Problem statement

Audits are invalidated whenever a work item's `updatedAt` changes after the audit time (`isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`). However, many changes do not affect the code or implementation that was audited (e.g., changing a comment, updating assignee). The audit skill should automatically inspect the changes since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or require a new one.

**Producer clarification:** The system should inspect anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it — description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not be unnecessarily re-audited when changes are irrelevant to the implementation.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited and whose changes are non-semantic.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item should stay ready unless changes actually affect the audit outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automatic re-instatement detection:** When `isAuditNotReadyFresh` returns `false` (audit flagged as stale), the system automatically inspects the changes made since `auditedAt` and decides whether to re-instate the audit or flag for re-audit.
2. **Change inspection covers key fields:** The inspection examines description, comments, audit text, dependencies, and commit messages for changes that could affect the audit outcome. Non-semantic changes (e.g., metadata-only updates) do not trigger re-audit.
3. **Re-instatement logic:** If changes are deemed non-semantic (no impact on audit outcome), the original audit is re-instated by resetting `updatedAt` to `auditedAt` (same pattern as `saveAuditResult`). If changes are semantic, the audit is flagged as needing re-run.
4. **Full project test suite passes** with new regression tests covering re-instatement of non-semantic changes and re-audit flag for semantic changes.

## Constraints

- Change confined to audit freshness logic in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the audit result management in the persistent store.
- No schema changes required.
- Must preserve existing audit behavior for items with no previous audit.
- Must be fully automatic — no operator intervention required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`. If false, the audit is treated as stale.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:1038`** — `saveAuditResult` resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`** — Audit results stored in SQLite; `getAllAuditResults` / `saveAuditResult` methods.

## Desired change

1. Create a new function `assessAuditInvalidate(changesSinceAudited, auditResult)` that inspects the delta between the audit time and current state.
2. The function should classify changes as semantic (affect audit outcome) or non-semantic (no impact).
3. For non-semantic changes, re-instate the audit (reset `updatedAt = auditedAt`).
4. For semantic changes, mark the audit as needing re-run.
5. Integrate into the `wl next` / TUI flow where audit freshness is checked.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), audit map builder, sorting logic
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Audit storage methods, `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — Sync merge logic
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — Audit command integration point
- `src/pi-audit.ts` — Pi audit module

## Related work

- **WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO** — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations (complementary; prevents timestamp churn, this handles post-invalidation review)
- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child of WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Established the audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** What counts as a semantic change is subjective. **Assumption:** Changes to description, comments, dependencies, and commit messages are semantic; changes to assignee, tags, priority, and sortIndex are non-semantic. Document the rule in code comments.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable invalidation policies. **Mitigation:** Keep this to the concrete scenarios identified; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Inspecting changes since audit could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Only run when freshness check fails; use efficient diff comparison.
- **Backward compatibility:** Existing audit behavior must be preserved for items with no previous audit result.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What specific change types should the audit skill inspect when deciding whether to re-instate an audit? — A: Anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it. So description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages etc. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: Should this be automatic (triggered when an invalidated audit is discovered) or manual (operator/producer-initiated)? — A: Automatic. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: How does this relate to WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations)? — A: Complementary — WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO prevents timestamp churn from invalidating audits, this item handles post-invalidation review to determine whether to re-instate or re-run. Source: interactive reply (producer).

# Dispatcher workspace has a useless blank pane

## Problem statement

When the Dispatcher workspace is created via `herdr workspace create --label Dispatcher --no-focus`, herdr automatically provisions a root pane. This root pane is persisted as the legacy `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` but is never adopted by any tab — the Dispatcher workspace sits with a blank, unused pane alongside the per-prefix tabs that carry the actual downtime dispatch work.

## Users

- **Downtime dispatcher operator** (Map/agent): the Dispatcher workspace should display only productive tabs, not a blank pane that adds clutter.
- **herdr interactive user**: a neutral workspace should show relevant panes only.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No blank root pane on first provision**: when the Dispatcher workspace is provisioned for the first time, the workspace's initial root pane must be adopted (as a tab or otherwise) rather than left blank — the workspace should contain only panes that serve the dispatch purpose.
2. **Idempotent re-provisioning**: on subsequent dispatch cycles, the existing workspace is reused without creating additional blank panes; if the root pane is closed, it is not replaced by a new blank pane.
3. **Per-prefix tab anchors preserved**: the existing tab-anchor mechanism (one tab per work-item prefix, persisted in `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`) continues to function correctly — each prefix still maps to a tab with an alive anchor pane.
4. **No regression to dispatch**: all downtime dispatch flows continue to route to the correct project CWD and pane placement; `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <pane-id>` works with the new layout.
5. **Test coverage**: existing `packages/herdr` test suite passes; new/updated tests cover the provision path.

## Constraints

- The fix must be within `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` and related files — do not modify `send-to-pi.sh` or `grid.py`.
- Must respect `--no-focus` semantics (never steal focus from the user's interactive workspace).
- Must be concurrency-safe (coordination lock pattern already established).
- Must not break the backward-compatible anchor file format (`downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` → `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`).

## Existing state

- `getDispatcherAnchor()` creates the workspace and stores the root pane ID in `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`.
- `getDispatcherTabAnchor()` creates per-prefix tabs inside the workspace, each with its own root pane.
- The workspace root pane (the anchor) is never adopted by any tab — it sits blank.
- Code: `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — `getDispatcherAnchor()` lines ~451–504, `createWorkspace` in deps ~98–113.

## Desired change

Provision the Dispatcher workspace such that the initial root pane is adopted as the first tab's pane (e.g. a generic "Downtime" tab or the first prefix tab). The root pane must remain alive to preserve the anchor file semantics.

**Validation against herdr 0.9.0 CLI:**
- `herdr workspace create` has no option to suppress the root pane — it is always created.
- `herdr pane move <pane-id> --tab <tab-id> --no-focus` can move a pane into an existing tab.
- `herdr pane move <pane-id> --new-tab --tab-label <label> --no-focus` can move a pane into a new tab.
- `herdr pane close` exists but must NOT be used for the anchor pane — closing it would break the `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <pane-id>` dispatch path, and `getDispatcherAnchor`'s stale detection would re-provision a new blank pane (infinite blank-pane loop).

**Recommended approach:**
1. After `deps.createWorkspace(DISPATCHER_WORKSPACE_LABEL)` returns `{ workspaceId, paneId }`, the root pane is at `paneId`.
2. Create a tab: `herdr tab create --workspace <ws-id> --label Downtime --no-focus`.
3. Move the root pane into the tab: `herdr pane move <rootPaneId> --tab <tabId> --no-focus`.
4. Close the tab's own root pane (created by `tab create`): `herdr pane close <tabRootPaneId>`.
5. Persist the anchor with the moved pane ID — it is now a tab pane.

**Constraints applied:** `--no-focus` on all CLI calls. Coordination lock pattern reused for concurrency safety.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — `getDispatcherAnchor()`, `createWorkspace()` in deps
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatch path, uses `getDispatcherAnchor` / `getDispatcherTabAnchor`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wiring of dispatcher anchor resolver
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — unit tests for anchor provisioning

## Related work

- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG** (completed): Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace regardless of project (C0: anchor-by-ID into dedicated Dispatcher workspace) — parent of the anchor provisioning work.
- **WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U** (completed): Implement dispatcher anchor provisioning (Anchor module) — child of C0, implemented the anchor.
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC** (open): Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace (route each prefix to its own tab) — child of C0, implemented per-prefix tabs.

## Headline

The Dispatcher workspace created by `herdr workspace create --label Dispatcher --no-focus` carries a blank root pane that is persisted but never adopted by any tab — it sits unused alongside the per-prefix dispatch tabs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `herdr workspace create` always creates a root pane. **Confirmed** — no CLI option to suppress.
- **Assumption**: The root pane can be adopted by a tab. **Confirmed** — `herdr pane move --tab` and `--new-tab --tab-label` provide the mechanism.
- **Assumption**: No code path depends on the workspace having a live root pane. **Confirmed** — consumers use the pane returned by `getDispatcherAnchor` / `getDispatcherTabAnchor` as the anchor target, not the workspace root.
- **Risk**: Closing the root pane would break dispatch and trigger a re-provision loop (stale detection → new blank pane). Avoided by adopting the pane into a tab instead.
- **Scope**: Minimal — only touch `getDispatcherAnchor` provision path. Per-prefix tab anchors (WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC) are unaffected.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'reused' mean — adopt the root pane as a tab, close it, or something else?" — Answer (code analysis): The root pane created by `herdr workspace create` is never adopted by any tab; tabs created via `herdr tab create` get their own root panes. Proposed fix: close the root pane after workspace creation, or adopt it as the first tab's pane. Source: code analysis of `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`.
- Q: "Can the root pane be closed via herdr CLI?" — Answer: `herdr pane close <pane-id>` exists and should work. Needs validation in implementation. Source: herdr CLI help.
- Q: "Should the per-prefix tab system be modified to adopt the root pane instead of closing it?" — Answer (preferred): If feasible, the root pane should be adopted as the first tab's pane. If not, closing it is the fallback. Source: code analysis — tabs always create new panes.
- Q: "What about the legacy `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` format?" — Answer: It should be deprecated in favour of the tab anchor format (`downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`). Source: existing code already uses both files.
- Q: "Can the root pane be moved into a tab via herdr CLI?" — Answer (validated): **Yes.** `herdr pane move <pane-id> --tab <tab-id> --no-focus` and `--new-tab --tab-label <label>` are available in herdr 0.9.0. **Preferred approach confirmed.** Source: `herdr pane move --help`, CLI verification.
- Q: "Is closing the root pane viable as a fallback?" — Answer (validated): **Not viable.** The anchor pane is used by `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <pane-id>` for dispatch. Closing it breaks dispatch and triggers `getDispatcherAnchor`'s stale-detection re-provision loop, creating a new blank pane. **Closing the anchor pane is not a viable approach.** Source: code analysis of `getDispatcherAnchor` stale-detection logic and `downtime-worker.ts` dispatch path.

# Intake Brief — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations

**Headline:** Audits are incorrectly invalidated by mechanical operations (re-sort, sync merges, and other timestamp-churning writes) that bump `updatedAt` without changing the work item's substantive state. This work item fixes all three paths so that audits are only invalidated by actual acceptance-criteria-relevant changes.

## Problem statement

Audits are being invalidated by non-semantic operations (re-sort, same-timestamp merge during sync, and other writes) that bump `updatedAt` without changing the work item's substantive state. The audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats these items as "edited after audit", causing passing audits to read as stale and items to linger in open queues unnecessarily.

**Producer clarification:** Audits should only be invalidated by (a) change in acceptance criteria, or (b) change in code impacting the acceptance criteria.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not appear as "needs re-audit" after mechanical operations like re-sort or sync.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited but invalidated only by timestamp churn.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical operations.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Re-sort does not invalidate audits:** `batchUpdateSortIndices` and the single-item re-sort path no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today. Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run re-sort, assert the audit is still fresh and `updatedAt` is unchanged.

2. **Same-timestamp merge does not invalidate audits:** `mergeSameTimestampItems` in sync no longer bumps `updatedAt` when the merged result equals one side (or converges without bumping). Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` synced repeatedly converge with no unbounded timestamp advancement; existing audit freshness preserved.

3. **General protection against non-semantic `updatedAt` bumps:** Mechanical operations (re-sort, sync merges, audit persistence) do not bump `updatedAt`. Substantive edits (status change, description edit, priority change) still bump `updatedAt` as today, correctly invalidating audits. The `saveAuditResult` pattern of resetting `updatedAt = auditedAt` is preserved. Regression test: audit an item, update its `assignee` or `tags` — audit should remain fresh.

4. **Full project test suite passes** with all new regression tests.

## Constraints

- Surgical changes confined to: `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` (batchUpdateSortIndices), `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` (mergeSameTimestampItems), and `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (if needed).
- No schema changes.
- Semantic edits must still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- Backward compatible: no CLI flag changes required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`** — `batchUpdateSortIndices` runs `UPDATE ... SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed.
- **`packages/shared/src/sync.ts:~L423`** — `mergeSameTimestampItems` sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:1269`** — `saveAuditResult` already resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.

## Desired change

1. In `batchUpdateSortIndices`, skip updating `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`.
2. In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field; converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side.
3. Consider extending the pattern in `saveAuditResult` (reset `updatedAt` to `auditedAt`) to other operations that should not invalidate audits, or implement a broader "semantic vs non-semantic change" detection mechanism. Document the chosen approach.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems` (line ~L423)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), recency scoring (line 2215)
- `tests/sync.test.ts` — Add regression tests for both failure modes
- `tests/database.test.ts` — Add reSort ordering tests for audit freshness

## Related work

- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child)
- **WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS** — Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely (child)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Boost audit-backed items in wl next sorting (established freshness rule)
- **WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V** — Concrete victim example: audited "Ready to close: Yes" now carries stale updatedAt from re-sort (referenced in WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable audit-invalidation policies or per-field granularity. **Mitigation:** Keep this item to the three concrete scenarios; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Checking whether a change is "semantic" vs "non-semantic" could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Simple whitelist of non-semantic operations (sortIndex updates, timestamp-only sync merges) is sufficient for now.
- **Regression risk:** Other parts of the system (TUI, herdr, sync) may depend on `updatedAt` being bumped for certain operations. **Mitigation:** Review all `updatedAt` references before changing; add integration tests for TUI selection, herdr dispatch, and sync convergence.
- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** The producer's definition of "change in acceptance criteria" may need clarification during implementation (e.g., should changing `assignee` or `priority` invalidate audits?). **Assumption:** Only status, description, and priority changes are semantic; metadata changes (tags, assignee, stage, issueType) are not. Document final rule in code comments.
- **Assumption:** The two child items (WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA, WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS) remain the primary victims; their existing acceptance criteria are subsumed by this broader fix.
- **Sync conflict risk:** Preventing `updatedAt` bumps in `mergeSameTimestampItems` may affect conflict resolution if both sides have divergent content. **Mitigation:** Preserve the existing merge semantics for content resolution; only skip the timestamp bump when the merged result equals one side.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which specific audit invalidation scenarios? — Answer (producer): All three — re-sort (WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA), same-timestamp merge (WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS), and any other write. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Bug fix or new feature? — Answer (producer): Bug fix — existing invalidation mechanisms are causing incorrect behaviour. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: When should audits be invalidated? — Answer (producer): Only by (a) change in acceptance criteria, or (b) change in code impacting the acceptance criteria. Source: interactive reply.
