# Worklog recovery extension crashes pi on stale ExtensionContext after session replacement (`_notifyFn`)

## Headline

The Worklog recovery extension must stop crashing the pi process when its
captured `ExtensionContext` goes stale after a session replacement/reload; a
stale `ctx.ui` in the asynchronous retry-notification path must skip the
notification instead of throwing an uncaught exception that aborts headless
pi runs (e.g. the SorraAgents audit runner) with a spurious
`provider_error: Connection error.`

## Problem Statement

`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` captures
the event-handler `ctx` into a module-level notify closure (`_notifyFn`). That
closure is later invoked asynchronously from the retry loop
(`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`, driven by `triggerInvisibleContinue`).
After pi replaces or reloads the session, `ctx.ui.notify()` throws
`This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload …`. Because
the call originates in a timer/async callback
(`process.processTicksAndRejections`), pi does not catch it, the Node process
exits, and the calling consumer surfaces `provider_error: Connection error.`

## Users

- **As a pi extension maintainer**, I want the recovery extension to be
  resilient to session replacement/reload, so that an in-flight recovery
  notification cannot crash the whole pi process.
  - *As a maintainer, I want the stale-ctx notification path to be defensively
    guarded and covered by a regression test, so that future refactors cannot
    reintroduce the uncaught exception.*
- **As an operator running headless/audit pi sessions**, I want my long-running
  audit runs to complete rather than be aborted after ~12 minutes by an
  extension crash, so that reliability data is trustworthy.
  - *As an operator, I want the extension to degrade gracefully (skip the
    notification) when the session has been replaced, so that a cosmetic
    UI notification never has process-level impact.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The stale-ctx uncaught exception no longer occurs: the retry notification
   path (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`) never throws when the session
   ctx has been replaced/reloaded; the notification is skipped when the ctx is
   stale.
2. A regression test is added: invoking the retry notification path with an
   invalidated/stale ctx asserts no throw (and that the notification is
   skipped).
3. The Worklog extension test suite passes with the change; the full project
   test suite must pass with the new changes.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically
   the recovery module header documenting the notify/ctx lifecycle.

## Constraints

- Do not change retry semantics otherwise (backoff, attempt counts, abort and
  session-generation guards, compaction-gate flow).
- Must not introduce npm dependencies beyond what the Worklog extension already
  uses.
- Follow existing Worklog extension conventions (module-level state pattern,
  `pi.on(...)` handlers, Vitest test layout under
  `lib/recovery/*.test.ts`).
- The guard must be defensive: completion/normal operation of the retry loop
  must not depend on UI notification succeeding.

## Existing State

- `register-recovery.ts` keeps module-level mutable state, including
  `_notifyFn` (line ~52), assigned from a captured handler `ctx` in the
  `agent_end` (line ~84) and `turn_end` (line ~88) handlers, and again in the
  `session_compact` handler (line ~212).
- `_notifyRetryAttempt` (line ~563) and other functions
  (`triggerCompactionContinue` ~462, `triggerCompactionGateRecovery`
  ~492/510/517) call `_notifyFn` asynchronously.
- `triggerInvisibleContinue` (line ~361) runs a `while (true)` retry loop,
  guarded by `interruptibleState.userAborted` and a
  `interruptibleState.sessionGeneration` comparison; it calls
  `_notifyRetryAttempt` (line ~408) after an interruptible sleep.
- `session_start` (line ~255) increments `interruptibleState.sessionGeneration`,
  resets retry/continuation state, but does **not** clear or re-bind
  `_notifyFn`.
- Existing recovery tests live alongside the source
  (`lib/recovery/*.test.ts`), e.g. `integration.test.ts`, `retry-loop.test.ts`,
  `compaction-gate.test.ts`, `session-compact.test.ts`, `retry-command.test.ts`.

## Desired Change

- `_notifyFn` must never throw after the ctx is invalidated. Re-bind/re-capture
  the notify function from the current handler ctx on each event that carries a
  ctx (and/or guard the call), so a stale ctx results in the notification being
  skipped rather than an uncaught exception.
- Consolidate the notify dispatch behind a single guarded helper (e.g. a
  `_safeNotify(message, level)` that wraps the captured `ctx.ui.notify` in a
  `try/catch`) so every call site (`_notifyRetryAttempt`,
  `triggerCompactionContinue`, `triggerCompactionGateRecovery`) shares the same
  stale-ctx protection.
- Consider clearing/re-capturing `_notifyFn` on `session_start` so a ctx from a
  replaced session is never retained, while a stale call still degrades to a
  no-op.
- Do not change retry semantics otherwise.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` —
  `_notifyFn` capture (lines ~52, ~84, ~88, ~212) and call sites
  (`_notifyRetryAttempt` ~563, ~462, ~492/510/517); add guarded notify helper and
  stale-ctx regression coverage hooks.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/*.test.ts` — new regression
  test (a new `notify-safety.test.ts` or an addition to
  `retry-loop.test.ts`/`integration.test.ts`) asserting a stale/invalidated ctx
  does not throw from the retry notification path.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — Error Recovery Module section, if it
  documents the notify lifecycle (verify and update as needed).

## Related Work

- **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F** (SorraAgents) — corrected root-cause analysis and
  handoff that originated this item. The SorraAgents side will separately make
  its own `pi-client` extensions stale-ctx-safe and track its audit-runner
  change.
- **WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF** — Automatically recover from appropriate server
  errors (completed; the parent retry-loop context that introduced the recovery
  module and `_notifyFn`).
- Evidence: stack trace `_notifyFn (register-recovery.ts:71:41)` →
  `_notifyRetryAttempt (register-recovery.ts:549:5)` →
  `triggerInvisibleContinue (register-recovery.ts:391:7)` →
  `process.processTicksAndRejections`; SorraAgents audit debug log
  `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl`
  (`context=parent`, `reason=provider_error`, `elapsed_seconds≈713`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption**: the crash is confined to the `_notifyFn` closure; direct
  `ctx.ui.notify(...)` calls inside `pi.on` handlers receive a fresh ctx per
  event and are not affected. If other async paths retain a ctx, they must be
  audited too (scope-creep risk — record as linked work items rather than
  expanding this fix).
- **Risk (scope creep)**: hardening *all* captured ctx usage across the
  recovery module could balloon the change. **Mitigation**: fix the identified
  `_notifyFn` path and any trivially adjacent retained-ctx call sites; record
  broader stale-ctx hardening as separate work.
- **Risk**: a `try/catch` that silently swallows all notification errors could
  mask genuine UI/registration bugs. **Mitigation**: keep the catch narrow and
  documented (stale-ctx is expected after replacement); do not alter control
  flow on caught errors.
- **Risk**: tests that exercise `registerRecoveryModule` depend on pi's event
  API and monkey-patching; the regression test should target the notify helper /
  capture lifecycle in isolation where possible to stay deterministic.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No clarifying questions were required. The seed context is the detailed handoff
from **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F** (SorraAgents), which supplies the goal, root cause,
stack-trace evidence, desired change, acceptance criteria, key files, and
related work. Repo inspection confirmed the described `_notifyFn` capture and
call sites in `register-recovery.ts` and the absence of any guard. No open
questions remain; no producer decision is needed to proceed to planning.

- Q: "Are there any open questions or ambiguities that block planning the
  fix?" — Answer (agent research, 2026-09-28): None. The fix is scoped by AC1
  ("notification is skipped when the ctx is stale") and the desired change
  ("re-bind/re-capture … and/or guard the call"). Design latitude (re-capture
  vs. guard vs. both) is intentionally left to implementation and does not
  change the ACs. Evidence: `register-recovery.ts` lines ~52–88, ~212, ~408,
  ~563; existing recovery tests under `lib/recovery/`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQDR51JO0037ISJ** – Eliminate unsafe as any casts in shortcut dispatch (detail view and duck-typing) (completed)
- **WL-0MSNKWLER003EGE0** – Auto-recover from JSON parse errors in audit processing (completed)
- **WL-0MUKH3DVA00488U0** – [test-failure] tests/herdr/form-dialog.test.ts — 6 legacy expectations stale after shell-escape change (WL-0MU7KEX65004X0U9) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, added, again, agent, analysis (+121 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: aborted, added, again, agent, appropriate (+103 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: added, again, agent, analysis, appropriate (+91 more)

# Downtime audits: prevent host-wide audit-slot / Local Proxy saturation from failing concurrent audits

## Problem statement

On 2026-09-26 at least four downtime-dispatched audits ran concurrently on a single host, saturating both the shared Local Proxy and the audit runner's host-wide audit concurrency slot (`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` in cheap-proxy mode). The audit for `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` failed on every Pi call after 90s and was aborted with no usable verdict. The existing per-instance active-audit detection and proxy-slot gating did not prevent this because they only guard dispatch within a single project's dispatcher — they cannot see audits dispatched by other projects' dispatchers on the same host.

## Users

- **Automated downtime agents** running Pi sessions during local-LLM idle time, which need a usable audit slot to complete their work.
- **Producers** reviewing audit outcomes, which cannot review an audit that was aborted due to infrastructure saturation rather than content issues.

## Existing state

- **Per-instance active-audit detection** (`WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB`): the audit tier is skipped when a non-stale `kind=audit` dispatch marker in `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` maps to an item still `in_progress`. This works within a single project but does not coordinate across projects.
- **Proxy-slot gating** in `downtime-worker.ts`: checks `available_slots`, `contention_queue_depth`, and per-slot ownership before dispatch.
- **Machine-wide coordination**: a single coordination file at `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` already provides cross-project communication for leader election and item offers, but does not track audit concurrency state.
- **Dispatch log**: per-project `downtime-dispatches.log` at `<cwd>/.worklog/` — separate from the machine-wide coordination file.

## Desired change

1. **Host-wide audit serialisation.** At most one audit-tier `/skill:audit` run should be actively executing per host — across herdr instances and projects. The dispatcher must either serialise audits or skip/defer audit dispatch while the audit runner's host-wide slot/queue is occupied or while the Local Proxy reports no free slots.
2. **Tolerate contention instead of failing.** When saturation is transient, the audit runner's admission wait should be sized so the run waits for a slot (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`) and/or the dispatch is retried later, rather than aborting with an infra-partial verdict.
3. **Regression test.** With a simulated occupied host-wide audit slot (or two dispatcher instances on one host), a second audit is not started; the candidate falls through to the next tier or is deferred.
4. **Observability.** Log a clear skip/defer reason (e.g. `audit-host-saturated`) that includes the number of concurrent audits and the audit-runner queue/slot state.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Host-wide audit serialisation.** Audit dispatch is serialised host-wide (single active audit run per host) or audit dispatch is skipped/deferred when the host-wide audit slot or Local Proxy slots are unavailable, including across projects and herdr instances. A new `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_HOST_SATURATION` mechanism (file-based or coordination-file-based) ensures at most one audit is active per host.
2. **Regression test.** A test proves a second concurrent audit is not started while one is active (simulated occupied slot / second instance), and that the candidate is deferred or falls through to another tier.
3. **Observability.** Contention produces a clear `audit-host-saturated` (or equivalent) skip/defer log line with the concurrent-audit count and queue/slot state.
4. **Documentation.** The host-wide coordination contract and its relationship to the existing per-instance active-audit detection and proxy-slot gating is documented.

## Constraints

- Must work with the existing machine-wide coordination infrastructure (`~/.herdr/downtime/`).
- Must be backward compatible — legacy dispatch logs without the new field should not break dispatch.
- The solution must not introduce additional I/O contention on the coordination mechanism.
- Must not change the Local Proxy's concurrency model.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Core dispatch logic, add host-wide audit serialisation gate.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit()` implementation, extend to read host-wide state.
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — Resolve coordination dir (may add host-audit tracking).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — Extend coordination data schema to include active audit tracking.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Add audit-saturation logging.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Regression test for host-wide serialisation.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8` — Audit dispatch tier (parent: creates the audit tier)
- `WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB` — Active-audit detection & audit-tier skip (per-instance serialisation)
- `WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66` — Active-audit single-flight tests (tests for the per-instance check)
- `WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY` — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (dispatch duplication)
- `WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN` — Single machine-wide downtime leader (coordination infrastructure)
- `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI` — Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane (evidence: "Failed due to audit concurrency saturation (temporary infrastructure issue — 43 items in queue)")

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What is the preferred mechanism for host-wide audit serialisation? — Answer (Map): Extend the existing machine-wide coordination infrastructure (`~/.herdr/downtime/`) with an audit serialisation marker. A dedicated file (e.g., `~/.herdr/downtime/active-audit`) is simpler than modifying the coordination file schema and avoids read-modify-write contention on the coordination file. Source: design analysis during intake.
- Q: Should the solution also handle the audit runner's 90s queue timeout, or only the dispatcher-side serialisation? — Answer (Map): The intake focuses on dispatcher-side serialisation (preventing dispatch when an audit is already running on the host). The audit runner's 90s timeout is a separate concern; the dispatch-level guard prevents saturation at the source. Source: intake analysis.
- Q: Scope: single-user hosts only, or multi-user? — Answer (Map): The existing machine-coordination contract explicitly states "single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) is out of scope" and resolves per-user. This item inherits that scope. Source: machine-coordination.ts, intake analysis.

# Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`

Discovered while investigating why the v1.0.16 release (WL-0MUJ3QN9C001QRZT) auto-closed **0 of 14** released `in_review` items.

## Problem

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` refuses to `wl close --force <parent>` whenever **any** descendant is not itself in the close-candidate set. The candidate set is built from `getCandidateItems()` (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`), which returns **only** `stage: in_review` items.

Descendants that are already terminal (`stage: done`) are therefore *not* candidates, so they are classified as "collateral" and the parent close is refused — even though a done child needs no action and re-affirming it is harmless.

## Evidence (release v1.0.16)

11 parents refused; their combined descendants classified:

- **29 already `stage: done`** → false-positive collateral (the defect)
- **1 `stage: in_review` with `needsProducerReview=true`** → legitimately skipped, but also counted as collateral
- **18 open/blocked non-terminal** (`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`) → refusal is correct (force-close must not sweep unfinished work)

Per parent:

| Parent | done children | non-terminal children | Refusal valid? |
|---|---|---|---|
| WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V | 9 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MSLW8GHQ0092PJK | 5 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q | 4 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514 | 3 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MSOYWZTH003JFVD | 3 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 | 1 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI | 1 | 4 | yes |
| WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28 | 3 | 2 | yes (includes npr=true child) |
| WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT | 0 | 1 | yes |
| WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 | 0 | 7 | yes |
| WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW | 0 | 5 | yes |

## Desired behaviour

1. The collateral-exclusion set must exclude descendants that are already terminal (`stage: done`), so a parent whose only non-candidate descendants are done is closable.
2. A descendant skipped solely because `needsProducerReview=true` should block the parent explicitly (reported as such), not be lumped under "collateral".
3. Genuine non-terminal descendants (`open`/`blocked`/`in_progress`) must still block the parent close.
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn` cover: (a) all-done descendants → parent closes; (b) one non-terminal descendant → parent refused; (c) npr=true descendant → parent refused with a distinct reason.
5. `npm run build` and existing suites pass.

## Notes

- The parent items in the "refusal valid" rows were advanced to `in_review` while children remain open/blocked — a separate tracking-hygiene concern.
- Related: SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H (AC9/AC10), SA-0MSAL2NQV0008HY5.

# Triage the 18 non-terminal children of v1.0.16-shipped parents

The v1.0.16 close step (WL-0MUJ3QN9C001QRZT) refused 5 `in_review` parents because each carries non-terminal children; `wl close --force` would sweep them. Investigation shows the 18 children split into **two very different classes**.

## Class A — shipped-but-unstaged (14 items)

Code is already committed and landed on `origin/dev` **and** `origin/main`; only the work-item stage is stale (`plan_complete`, `open`/`blocked`). Recommended: advance to `in_review` with a passing audit, then close as shipped.

| WL-0MUDEIYUB008FFC2 | 779533a1 | WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW |
| WL-0MUDEJU9Z004UO2W | af685859 | WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW |

| WL-0MUDENSX6008KVGH | 4ff613c8 | WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW |
| WL-0MU72BUJ70032OQE | be420a3e | WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT |
| WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F | 555e41b6 | WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28 |

## Class B — genuinely unimplemented (4 items)

No commits, still `intake_complete`. Recommended: re-parent to a new successor epic (e.g. "Herdr hydrator — remaining scope") so the shipped parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI can close without sweeping them.

- WL-0MTF5WNZV003JKMJ — Docs: herdr hydrator section

## Why the parents were blocked

- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI: blocked by Class B children.

## Root cause / prevention

Parents reached `in_review` (`status: completed`) while their children were still non-terminal. Investigate whether the audit-runner `inherited_pass` bypass (SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0 in SorraAgents) allowed this, and add a guard so a parent cannot advance to `in_review` with non-terminal children (or record an explicit partial-ship decision).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Class A children advanced to `in_review`/`completed` with audits, then closed as shipped; their parents (WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4, WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW, WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT, WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28) transition to `stage: done`.
2. Class B children re-parented to a successor epic and the parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI closed, with no non-terminal child swept.
3. Prevention measure implemented or explicitly deferred with a linked work item.
4. `wl doctor` reports no new issues for the affected items.

# Prune and rotate stale audit_debug JSONL files across worklog stores

**Issue type:** chore (maintenance/tooling) · **Priority:** critical · **Parent:** none

## Problem statement

Legacy `audit_debug_*.jsonl` forensic dumps have accumulated in worklog stores
on this host — ContextHub `.worklog` holds **48 files / 12.5 GB** (store total
13 GB) and `open_source_llm/.worklog` holds **33 files / 11.3 GB** (store total
11 GB), with single files up to ~1.9 GB last written 2026-08-01. A further
**2.5 GB** sits under `~/.audit_debug/`. These files make recursive greps read
multi-GB inputs (observed ~4.4 GB read, 12+ minutes, ~48% CPU) and inflate every
worklog/audit operation. No automation prunes either location, so the growth is
silent and unbounded.

## Users

- **Agents/operators running greps and audits on this host** — "As an agent
  running quality gates, I want stale debug dumps pruned and size-bounded
  automatically so scans stay fast and predictable."
- **Maintainer/producer** — "As a maintainer, I want retention enforced by
  automation (not one-off manual cleanups) so disk usage cannot silently reach
  tens of GB again."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Retention sweep is implemented and unit-tested.** A repo-local script at
   `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` discovers `audit_debug_*.jsonl` files
   under every `~/projects/*/.worklog/` store and under `~/.audit_debug/**`, and
   selects for removal those older than `--older-than` days (default **7**) **or**
   larger than `--max-size` MB (default **50**). It is dry-run by default;
   `--apply` performs deletion. Pytest tests cover: age boundary, size boundary,
   non-matching filenames are never touched, missing root is a no-op, dry-run
   changes nothing, and `--apply` deletes exactly the selected set.
   *Verification:* `pytest tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py` passes.
2. **Legacy backlog is reclaimed.** Running the sweep with `--apply` removes all
   legacy `audit_debug_*.jsonl` files from ContextHub `.worklog` (48 → 0) and
   `open_source_llm/.worklog` (33 → 0), reclaiming **≥ 20 GB**. Before/after
   aggregate counts and `du -sh` figures are recorded as a work-item comment.
   *Verification:* `ls <store>/audit_debug_*.jsonl` returns nothing for both
   stores; total reclaimed size recorded.
3. **Recurrence is prevented by automation.** A daily cron entry (installed by
   an idempotent `scripts/install-audit-log-hygiene.sh` helper, or documented as
   a copy-paste `crontab -l` snippet when auto-install is declined) runs the
   sweep with `--apply` and appends to a bounded log under `~/.audit_debug/`.
   Re-running the sweep immediately afterwards reports **no candidates**
   (idempotent). A `--check` mode exits non-zero when the post-sweep total
   debug-log footprint exceeds a configurable budget, suitable for manual or
   hook-driven use. *Verification:* unit tests assert exit codes for `--check`
   under/over budget; a second `--apply` run reports zero candidates.
4. **Policy and runbook are documented.** A docs page
   (`docs/dev/audit-debug-log-retention.md`) states the retention policy
   (locations, thresholds, dry-run/apply semantics, cron install and removal,
   safety guarantees, and the `~/.audit_debug` vs legacy `.worklog` distinction)
   and is linked from the relevant docs index. *Verification:* file exists and
   is linked; documented commands are copy-paste runnable.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes** (code
   comments, README/docs site entries) **and the full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Destructive-by-explicit-flag only.** Default is dry-run; deletion requires
  `--apply`. Only files matching `audit_debug_*.jsonl` are ever considered.
- **Never touch tracked or live data.** `.worklog/*` is git-ignored, but the
  sweep must not touch `worklog.db`/WAL/SHM, `config.yaml`, worktrees, or any
  non-debug file. Live SQLite worklog data is unaffected.
- **Repo boundaries.** Do **not** edit the SorraAgents-owned audit skill
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit`, `skill/audit`) or other agent-infrastructure
  directories as part of this item. The existing
  `audit/scripts/cleanup_debug_logs.py` (14-day retention over `~/.audit_debug`,
  dry-run default) is **referenced, not forked**. Upstreaming the `~/.audit_debug`
  half into that skill is a follow-up, not scope.
- Deletions must be resilient to `OSError` (skip and continue, never abort the
  whole sweep) and must emit an audit line per removed file.
- Only aggregate counts/sizes are recorded in work-item comments — never log
  contents (forensic data may include provider payloads).
- **Scope-creep guard:** the broader machine-hygiene skill
  (WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ) and any pre-commit/pre-push enforcement beyond a
  documented optional `--check` call are out of scope; record as follow-ups.

## Existing state

- `audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents `skill/audit`) now writes debug logs to
  `~/.audit_debug/<project-slug>/` (`_debug_log_dir`/`_default_debug_log_path`)
  and deletes them on a successful run (`_remove_debug_log`). New logs therefore
  no longer land in `.worklog/`, so the 24 GB in the two worklog stores is stale
  legacy data that will not regrow.
- `cleanup_debug_logs.py` already sweeps `~/.audit_debug` (files >14 days,
  dry-run default, `--apply` to delete) but is **not automated** and does **not**
  cover legacy `.worklog` locations.
- No cron entry exists for audit-log pruning (only an `llm-wiki` job is present).
- `.gitignore` ignores `.worklog/*`, so legacy files are untracked and safe to
  delete; repo scan helpers (`audit/scripts/scan.py`) already exclude
  `**/audit_debug_*.jsonl` and `.audit_debug/**`.

## Desired change

1. Add a self-contained retention script (Python, stdlib-only) with the
   discovery, age/size selection, dry-run/apply, and `--check` semantics above.
2. Add pytest coverage for selection, safety, idempotence, and exit codes.
3. Add an idempotent cron-install helper plus documentation; optionally surface
   a `--check` call from an existing hook as a non-fatal warning.
4. Reclaim the existing backlog with a recorded before/after.
5. Document the policy/runbook.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` — **new**: discovery + age/size selection +
  dry-run/`--apply`/`--check`; mirrors `cleanup_debug_logs.py` conventions.
- `scripts/install-audit-log-hygiene.sh` — **new**: idempotent cron entry
  installer (with `--remove`), logging to `~/.audit_debug/hygiene-cron.log`.
- `tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py` — **new**: pytest unit tests over a
  temp directory tree (age boundary, size boundary, dry-run, apply, check mode).
- `docs/dev/audit-debug-log-retention.md` — **new**: policy + runbook.
- `.gitignore` — **review**: confirm `.worklog/*` already covers these paths
  (expected: no change needed).
- `.githooks/pre-push` — **optional**: non-fatal `--check` warning (only if the
  producer opts in; otherwise out of scope).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — placement:** tooling lives in ContextHub `scripts/` (this
  item's home repo) and is machine-scoped via `~/projects/*` discovery, rather
  than editing the SorraAgents-owned audit skill. *Open to producer redirection.*
- **Assumption — delete over archive:** the seed permits "archive … or delete";
  we delete, because these are transient forensics already documented as such by
  the audit skill and the reclaimed volume (≥20 GB) is the point. If cold
  storage is required, add a `--archive-dir` (gzip) variant before deletion.
- **Risk — over-broad glob.** A loose pattern could match non-debug files; the
  `audit_debug_*.jsonl` prefix/suffix guard and tests mitigate this.
- **Risk — deleting useful forensics.** Retention is age/size based; files
  newer than the threshold are kept. The 7-day/50 MB defaults are aggressive but
  match the seed; they are CLI-configurable.
- **Risk — scope creep** into machine hygiene / hooks. Guarded above; extras
  become linked follow-up items.
- **Assumption — default retention:** 7 days / 50 MB per the seed, with a
  total-footprint `--check` budget (proposed: 5 GB) documented and configurable.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ** — Create a machine-hygiene skill that evaluates
  performance pressure and proposes remediations (explicitly references this
  item as a root cause; the manual analysis that discovered the runaway grep).
- **WL-0MKTLALHV0U51LWN** — Reduce sync output; add rotating logs (completed;
  precedent for rotating-log handling in `wl sync`).
- SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/cleanup_debug_logs.py` — existing retention
  sweep for `~/.audit_debug` (referenced, not forked).
- SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — already excludes
  `audit_debug_*.jsonl` / `.audit_debug/**` from scans.
- SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_debug_log_dir` (moved
  logs out of `.worklog/`), `_remove_debug_log` (deletes on success).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No blocking interview was required** — the seed context (work item
  description) specified the strategy, thresholds (7 days / 50 MB), locations,
  and automation mechanism (cron) sufficiently to draft this brief.
- Q: Where should the retention tooling live, given the audit skill is owned by
  the SorraAgents repo? — Answer (agent, documented assumption): this item's home
  repo, ContextHub `scripts/`, with machine-scoped discovery; marked as an
  assumption open to producer redirection. Source: repo inspection
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit` → `SorraAgents/skill/audit`; ContextHub `skill/`
  has no audit skill) + work-item seed.
- Q: Archive to cold storage or delete? — Answer (seed context): either is
  acceptable; **delete** selected as the default with an `--archive-dir` escape
  hatch if cold storage is later required. Source: work item description
  ("archive older files to cold storage or delete").
- Q: What automation mechanism? — Answer (seed context): **cron-based** daily
  `--apply` sweep, plus a `--check` mode for manual/hook use. Source: work item
  description ("implement a cron-based rotation").
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **WL-0MSAWAQNM006PAVJ** – Plugin delegates to shared resolver (completed)

# Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion

## Problem statement

Pi agent sessions launched in Herdr panes run `pi` in **interactive** mode with
an initial prompt (`packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`). When a skill
completes it emits a `</end_session>` marker, but nothing consumes that marker:
the interactive REPL simply waits for the next input, so the pane and its
~200 MB pi process stay alive forever. Over hours these abandoned sessions
accumulate — the operator observed **50 concurrent pi sessions / ~12.4 GB RSS
with ages up to 18+ hours**, contributing to severe CPU oversubscription
(load ~3× cores). Nothing transitions the session to a closed state on skill
completion, and there is no lifecycle hook that reaps sessions whose agent died
without emitting the marker.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — wants completed agent panes to disappear on their
  own so the machine is not oversubscribed and panes do not need manual pruning.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — spawns intake/plan/audit/risk-effort panes for every
  dispatched item; if those panes never close, the dispatcher floods the host.
- **Agents** — need their session to end cleanly (lease released, pane torn
  down) once their task and report are complete, without an operator click.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when a dispatched `/skill:intake` or `/skill:plan` session
  finishes and writes its `</end_session>` report, I want the pane to close
  automatically so idle sessions do not accumulate.
- As a producer, I want an agent that stops to ask me a question (no
  `</end_session>`) to keep its pane open so I can answer it, but an agent whose
  process died silently to be cleaned up.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — graceful auto-close on completion.** When a session's final
   assistant message's concatenated text, `.rstrip()`-ed, ends with
   `</end_session>`, the pane is closed programmatically by the shared closure
   script so the process exits, the pane is torn down, and the proxy model
   lease is released — with no operator action. (Mechanism revised in planning:
   an in-process `agent_end`/`agent_settled` hook is NOT used, because the SDK
   exposes no `agent_settled` event and `agent_end` proved unreliable; the
   scheduled closure script owns this — see Appendix Q5.) Metric: a unit test
   with a fixture session whose last assistant text ends with the marker asserts
   a close is requested exactly once; an end-to-end check shows the pane closes
   within one reaper interval.
2. **AC2 — no false positives.** No close is requested when the final
   assistant message does not end with the marker — including a `</end_session>`
   quoted mid-message, a question-ended session, an aborted run, and a run that
   ended in a non-retryable error. Metric: negative-path unit tests for each
   case assert zero close requests, and an item with
   `needsProducerReview=true` is never auto-closed.
3. **AC3 — marker-less sessions are reaped (fail-closed).** Sessions whose agent
   died or was killed without emitting the marker do not linger indefinitely: a
   liveness/idle reaper closes panes whose agent process is gone or idle beyond
   a configurable threshold (default 30 minutes, per producer decision), while **never**
   closing a pane that is actively working, has live child processes, or has
   `needsProducerReview=true`. Metric: table-driven classifier tests plus an
   integration check on a synthetic abandoned pane.
4. **AC4 — `implement` panes remain excluded** from automatic close, preserving
   the AC6 precedent of `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` unless the producer explicitly
   changes the policy. Metric: a test asserts an `implement` pane is never
   auto-closed.
5. **AC5 — child processes are not orphaned.** When a session exits or is
   terminated, its spawned children (e.g. audit/plan runners) are terminated
   with it, so none are reparented to PID 1. Metric: an integration test spawns
   a long-running child in a session-scoped process group, terminates the
   session, and asserts the child does not survive.
6. **AC6 — one shared idle/completion classifier.** The automatic hook and the
   `pane-triage` skill (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`) consume a single
   marker-detection + liveness helper, so the two mechanisms cannot diverge.
   Metric: both call the shared module; its classifier is covered by
   table-driven tests (marker at end accepted; marker mid-message rejected).
7. **AC7 — tests and documentation.** Unit and integration tests are added for
   every path. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`, and any
   relevant `docs/` entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Constraints

- Must not close a pane that is actively working **or** awaiting a producer
  answer.
- Mechanism (revised in planning): closure is performed by a scheduled,
  out-of-process closure script that reads session logs — NOT by an in-process
  `agent_end` hook. The script must never race the existing `agent_end`
  recovery/compaction flow: it only closes a pane whose session is demonstrably
  settled (idle beyond the threshold, or its agent process is gone).
- The existing downtime auto-close logic (`pane-lifecycle.ts`,
  `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN`) must remain intact and must not double-handle or race
  the new closure script; both must be idempotent.
- Auto-close must be configurable/overridable (threshold, on/off) so an operator
  can disable it without editing code.
- Headless modes (JSON/RPC) must be unaffected; gate UI-facing behaviour to TUI
  mode as `herdr-agent-state.ts` already does.
- Never close the invoking/current operator pane.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` runs `pi` (interactive) with an
  initial prompt; on `pi` exit its `EXIT` trap calls
  `release-lease-on-exit.mjs` and Herdr tears the pane down when the primary
  process exits. **The gap is that `pi` never exits.**
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/` is the auto-loaded pi extension
  (`index.ts` wires activity indicator, model display, session health,
  guardrails, skill-path, recovery, lease release). It hooks `agent_end`,
  `session_shutdown`, `agent_start` and `turn_end`. Note: the pi SDK exposes
  **no** `agent_settled` event (verified against
  `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` `ExtensionAPI` types), so an
  `agent_settled`-based hook is not implementable as originally drafted.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` inspects
  the last assistant message on `agent_end` — a precedent for reading final
  output, and a coordination point so recovery finishes before shutdown.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` classifies **dispatched** panes by
  worklog stage and closes everything except `implement`; it only covers panes
  recorded in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, so manually opened and
  marker-less panes are never reaped.
- `~/.pi/agent/extensions/herdr-agent-state.ts` reports `idle`/`working`/
  `blocked` to Herdr but never closes anything.
- The report helper (`~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  appends the canonical `</end_session>` marker and is emitted by every skill's
  end-of-session report.
- Observed evidence: 44–50 live `pi` processes (~200 MB RSS each), sessions with
  completed work still alive, and orphaned `audit_runner` children reparented to
  PID 1.

## Desired change

Build an out-of-process, script-driven session-closure capability (revised in
planning — see Appendix Q5):

1. A **shared closure classifier** (pure logic, table-driven tests) that
   decides, for one session/pane: idle-with-marker, idle-without-marker
   (agent process gone or idle beyond the 30-minute threshold), active, or
   never-close (`implement`, `needsProducerReview=true`, invoking pane).
2. A **closure script** (CLI) that scans herdr panes, classifies each via the
   shared classifier, and closes eligible panes idempotently, writing a ledger.
   This is the programmatic handler; it does not depend on the unreliable
   in-process `agent_end` event.
3. The script is **scheduled** to run periodically (herdr downtime-worker tick
   or equivalent) with on/off + threshold configuration, and is idempotent
   against the existing `pane-lifecycle.ts` dispatch monitor.
4. Session-scoped child processes are terminated on closure so none are
   orphaned to PID 1.
5. The **`pane-triage` skill** (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`) reuses the same
   classifier/script rather than re-deriving idle state from the session log
   (coordination: comment + dependency edge).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` — **new**: shared closure classifier (marker detection + liveness + close eligibility). Pure, no I/O.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.test.ts` — **new**: table-driven classifier tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — **new**: closure script orchestration (scan → classify → close → ledger), injectable I/O.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts` — **new**: fixture-based reaper tests (exclusions, idempotence, no-op).
- `packages/herdr/src/process-group.ts` + `.test.ts` — **new**: session-scoped child-process teardown.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — existing dispatch-pane classifier; keep intact, de-duplicate against the new closure script.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — periodic wiring/scheduling of the closure script.
- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` — reference only (exit/lease-release path).
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document the closure script and its configuration.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py` — reference only (marker source).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `</end_session>` is the single canonical terminal signal and
  is always the final line of a completed skill report.
- **Risk — premature close.** An in-process `agent_end` hook could race
  recovery/compaction. Mitigated by the planning decision to close
  out-of-process from a scheduled script that requires the session to be
  settled (agent process gone, or idle beyond the 30-minute threshold).
- **Risk — false-positive close** of an interactive session mid-conversation;
  mitigated by strict final-message marker matching plus negative-path tests.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Orphaned-child reaping and the marker-less reaper
  overlap existing work; if either grows large it should become a child item
  rather than inflate this fix.
- **Risk — double handling.** The downtime `pane-lifecycle` monitor may race
  the new closure script; both must be idempotent and the winner must be
  deterministic.
- **Risk — marker-less session misclassification.** A genuinely working agent
  that is silent for >30 minutes could be reaped. Mitigated by requiring the
  agent process to be gone OR the idle threshold to be exceeded, plus
  live-child-process and `needsProducerReview` guards.

## Related work

- `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` — Create pane-triage skill: gated close of idle panes (manual complement; reuses the shared classifier/script — see Appendix Q1/Q5).
- `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` — Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement (precedent; `implement` exception).
- `WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN` — Implement auto-close logic with implement exception.
- `WL-0MSGI7UIH008USVB` — Herdr plugin: release the Local Proxy model lease when a pi session is closed (exit/release path).
- `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` — Create a machine-hygiene skill that evaluates performance pressure (orphaned audit_runners, stale servers).
- `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM).
- `WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO` — Fix orphaned ContextHub node processes that never exit after worktree cleanup.
- `WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O` — Auto-continue after mid-session compaction (session lifecycle precedent).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Deferral to the pane-triage skill (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`).**
  Should this item defer to pane-triage, or own the automatic lifecycle fix?
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-27):** Keep both. This item owns the automatic
  fix; pane-triage remains the approval-gated manual complement. Rationale:
  pane-triage's idle test is the same `</end_session>` marker and it never
  closes anything unattended, so it cannot prevent accumulation (50
  sessions/18h accumulated despite the operator being available), and it is
  blind to sessions whose agent died without emitting the marker. **Final:
  no deferral.** The producer further directed that a *script* perform the
  programmatic closure and that pane-triage reuse that script so the two
  cannot diverge (see Q5). This supersedes the earlier OPEN QUESTION.
- **Q2 — Marker-less / crashed sessions.**
  Is a gated manual close sufficient, or is an automatic liveness/idle reaper
  required? **Answer (producer):** automatic, fail-closed reaper is required
  (AC3), because marker-less sessions are invisible to pane-triage and
  dominated the observed backlog. **Final: automatic reaper.**
- **Q3 — Orphaned child-process cleanup (AC5) scope.**
  In scope here or a separate child item? **Answer (producer):** focus here —
  AC5 stays in this item (not split out). **Final: in scope.**
- **Q5 — Closure mechanism (in-process hook vs out-of-process script).**
  `agent_end` was found unreliable and the SDK exposes no `agent_settled`
  event. **Answer (producer):** do not rely on `agent_end`; write a script
  that programmatically handles the closures, and coordinate with
  `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` so the pane-triage skill uses the script. **Final:
  out-of-process, scheduled closure script + shared classifier.**
- **Q6 — Idle threshold for the marker-less reaper.** **Answer (producer):**
  30 minutes. **Final: default 30 minutes, configurable.**
- **Q7 — Placement of the shared script.** **Open (assumption).**
  Recommended: ContextHub `packages/herdr/` (the pure classifier, CLI and
  scheduler live beside the existing `pane-lifecycle.ts`, and herdr's build
  and tests already cover them); the pane-triage skill (SorraAgents
  `skill/pane-triage/`) invokes the script. Alternative: place the CLI inside
  `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/scripts/` (crosses repos). Recorded as an
  assumption to validate at implementation.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-09-27** — Initial decomposition. Revised AC1/AC2/AC3 and the
  mechanism from an in-process `agent_end` hook to a scheduled, out-of-process
  closure script + shared classifier (producer decision, Appendix Q5/Q6);
  resolved Appendix Q1–Q3; split work into test-first child items. Session:
  see session-logging comment.
- **Q4 — Does `</end_session>` align with the session-close lifecycle?**
  **Answer (agent research):** Partially. It is the correct primary signal for
  graceful completions, but the pane-triage model misses sessions that died
  without emitting it. Evidence: live idle `pi` REPLs with completed work, plus
  `audit_runner` children reparented to PID 1 (parent died, no marker).
  Source: process inspection, `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/*`,
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP** – Show complete, right-aligned model name on footer Line 3 (remove 30-col truncation) (completed)
- **WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514** – Align wl init with SorraAgents install: delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup instead of duplicating (completed)
- **WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO** – In-flight guard: Herdr-head and normal scan paths (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0msgi7uih008usvb, abandoned, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+350 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: aborted, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac5 (+293 more)

# Machine-Hygiene Skill — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

A global `machine-hygiene` skill that automates the manual performance-pressure analysis performed on 2026-09-27 (which resolved load 44 on 16 cores, CPU pressure 88.8%, a runaway 4.4 GB grep, orphaned `audit_runners` and stale vite servers). The skill provides a repeatable, safe diagnostic-and-remediation workflow for hosts running many concurrent pi agent sessions and test suites. It never acts autonomously without explicit producer approval.

**Headline:** Create the `machine-hygiene` global skill with a 6-step diagnostic-and-remediation workflow, configurable thresholds, before/after metric tables, and explicit approval gates before any destructive action.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — needs an automated, safe way to identify and resolve machine performance pressure without manually inspecting processes.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — can invoke the skill to auto-diagnose machine health during idle periods and report actionable findings.
- **Agents** — benefit from a cleaner, more responsive host machine when running multiple sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Global skill structure.** A skill named `machine-hygiene` exists under `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` with a `SKILL.md`, a `scripts/` directory, and tests per skill-authoring conventions. It is discoverable via `/skill: machine-hygiene`.

2. **AC2 — Diagnostic evaluation (Step 1).** The skill collects and renders a **before table** with the following metrics: load average (vs. core count), `/proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}` (percentages), free memory and swap usage, process and thread counts, per-command aggregate RSS (top 10), runnable process count, and stale device detection (zombie processes, stale files/locks). Each metric is classified as **low** (green), **warning** (amber), or **critical** (red) using configurable thresholds.

3. **AC3 — Pressure analysis (Steps 2–3).** The skill describes the primary pressures — identifying which processes/resources contribute most, their attributable ancestry (parent processes, systemd units, session IDs), and proposes concrete remediation actions (kill, renice, prune stale sessions, pace concurrent work), each with target PIDs/paths and expected impact.

4. **AC4 — Approval gate (Step 4).** The skill **stops** and presents findings to the operator/producer, awaiting explicit approval. No destructive action (kill, delete, modify) is taken before approval.

5. **AC5 — Conditional action (Step 5).** Only the explicitly approved subset of proposed actions is executed. The skill tracks which actions were approved vs. declined and reports accordingly.

6. **AC6 — After table (Step 6).** An **after table** is rendered alongside the before table showing current state for each metric, with per-metric priority annotations, and reports residual/legitimate load (e.g., active test suites, ongoing sessions).

7. **AC7 — Threshold configuration.** Low/warning/critical thresholds are configurable via a YAML config file (`~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/config.yaml`) with documented sensible defaults. Defaults cover: CPU pressure (>70% warning, >85% critical), memory usage (>80% warning, >95% critical), I/O pressure (>50% warning, >80% critical), load average (>cores*0.7 warning, >cores*1.5 critical), zombie processes (>5 warning, >20 critical).

8. **AC8 — Tests.** Tests cover: threshold classification logic, the approval-gate refusal path (verify no destructive action without approval), metric collection on synthetic/fixture data, and config-file override behavior.

9. **AC9 — Documentation.** The skill is documented in `SKILL.md` with invocation examples, and is discoverable via `/skill: machine-hygiene`.

10. **AC10 — Full suite and documentation freshness.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, `SKILL.md`, and any relevant `docs/` entries), and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only by default.** Destructive actions (kill, delete, modify) are gated behind explicit operator/producer approval.
- **No direct .worklog mutation.** Any work-item side effects must use `wl` commands.
- **Reusable across projects.** Global skill under `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/`, with tests per skill-authoring conventions.
- **Process management scope only.** The skill focuses on process management (kill, renice, prune, pace). Resource-limiting via cgroups/systemd is out of scope.
- **Configurable thresholds.** Thresholds are configurable via YAML with sensible defaults.

## Existing State

- Manual machine-health analysis was performed on 2026-09-27, resolving load 44 on 16 cores, CPU pressure 88.8%, a runaway 4.4 GB grep, orphaned `audit_runners`, and stale vite servers.
- Related root causes are documented in:
  - `WL-0MUJL0PTS009MC8F` — debug-log rotation (audit debug log hygiene)
  - `WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS` — session close lifecycle (orphaned sessions, abandoned panes)
- Existing skills provide patterns: `cleanup` (branch pruning), `context-audit` (context measurement), and `heartbeat` (automated work monitoring).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — **new**: skill entry point with the 6-step workflow and approval gate
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/evaluate.py` — **new**: main entry point; orchestrates Steps 1–6
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py` — **new**: collects and classifies performance metrics (load, pressure, memory, swap, procs, RSS)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py` — **new**: analyses primary pressures, identifies root causes, proposes remediation actions
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/actions.py` — **new**: executes approved remediation actions (kill, renice, prune)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/tables.py` — **new**: renders before/after tables with status symbols
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — **new**: configurable thresholds with documented defaults
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — **new**: threshold classification and metric collection tests
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` — **new**: pressure analysis and remediation proposal tests
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_approval_gate.py` — **new**: approval-gate refusal tests

## Related Work

- `WL-0MUJL0PTS009MC8F` — Audit debug log retention (related: log-related resource consumption)
- `WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS` — Session close lifecycle (related: orphaned sessions, abandoned panes contributing to pressure)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/cleanup` — Branch cleanup skill (pattern reference for skill structure)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit` — Context measurement skill (pattern reference for metric collection)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/heartbeat` — Automated work monitoring (pattern reference for scheduled analysis)

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The skill runs on Linux with access to `/proc/pressure/` and standard process inspection tools (`ps`, `top`). Non-Linux platforms may need adaptation (documented as a follow-up).
- **Risk — false positives on RSS aggregation.** Per-command RSS grouping can be noisy when many instances of the same binary run under different names. Mitigation: group by process name (not command line) and show top 10 with individual PID breakdowns.
- **Risk — killing the wrong process.** Kill actions must include process ancestry verification (parent, session, uid) before execution. The approval gate requires operator confirmation for each kill.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Resource-limiting (cgroups, systemd) and I/O throttling are tempting but would significantly expand scope. Explicitly out of scope.
- **Risk — stale device detection accuracy.** Zombie processes and stale locks can be legitimate (e.g., during test teardown). The skill should flag rather than auto-remediate these; flagged items are always presented for approval, never auto-executed.
- **Scope-creep opportunity:** A scheduled cron-based auto-hygiene mode (runs at intervals, logs to a file) — captured as a linked follow-up, not in scope. This could be a separate `WL` child item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Skill name and location.** Should the skill be called `host-hygiene`, `perf-hygiene`, or `machine-hygiene`, and should it be global or project-scoped? **Answer (producer):** Proceed with `machine-hygiene` as a global skill under `~/.pi/agent/skills/`. **Final: `machine-hygiene`, global.**
- **Q2 — Threshold configuration.** Should thresholds be hardcoded, configurable, or both? **Answer (producer):** Proceed with configurable via YAML with sensible defaults. **Final: YAML config with documented defaults.**
- **Q3 — Action types beyond kill/prune.** Should the skill recommend resource-management actions like `nice`/`renice` or cgroup limits? **Answer (producer):** Focus on process management (kill, renice, prune, pace). cgroup/systemd resource-limiting is out of scope. **Final: process management only.**

# CLI: treat `--parent null` as detach instead of creating a bogus `WL-NULL` parent

**As a** CLI/TUI user managing work-item hierarchy, **I want** `--parent null` to detach an item (set `parentId` to `null`), **so that** detaching a work item is discoverable and does not silently corrupt the hierarchy with an invalid parent reference.

## Problem

`normalizeCliId()` (`src/cli-utils.ts`) turns any bare token into `<PREFIX>-<TOKEN>`:

```ts
if (trimmed.includes('-')) return trimmed.toUpperCase();
return `${prefix}-${trimmed.toUpperCase()}`;
```

So `wl update <id> --parent null` produces the literal parent id **`WL-NULL`**, which does not exist. The item ends up with a dangling parent link rather than becoming top-level. The only working detach syntax today is the undocumented `--parent ""`.

### Evidence

- Reproduced live during the v1.0.16 release follow-up: `wl update WL-0MTF5WNZV003JKMJ --parent null` set `parentId = "WL-NULL"` (fixed with `--parent ""`).
- Two pre-existing items still carry the artefact: **WL-0MLGTKNKF14R37IA** and **WL-0MLGTKO880HYPZ2R** (both `done`, `parentId = "WL-NULL"`).
- `wl show WL-NULL` → "Work item not found".

## Desired behaviour

1. `wl update <id> --parent null` (case-insensitive) detaches the item: `parentId` becomes `null`, exit code 0, no `WL-NULL` written.
2. The same sentinel is accepted by `wl create` (`--parent null` == top-level item, the default).
3. Existing detach syntax `--parent ""` continues to work unchanged (backwards compatible).
4. A genuinely invalid parent id (e.g. a non-existent `WL-XXXX`) still fails as today — no behaviour change there.
5. `--parent` help text documents the detach form; `CLI.md` and `EXAMPLES.md` document it.
6. `wl doctor` detects dangling `WL-NULL` (or any non-existent) parent references and proposes a fix; the two known items are remediated.

## Suggested implementation

- Add a small `normalizeParentId(value, prefix)` helper (in `src/cli-utils.ts`) that maps case-insensitive `null` / `none` / `nil` / `-` (and empty string) to `null`, otherwise delegates to `normalizeCliId()`.
- Use it at both call sites: `src/commands/update.ts` (`parentCandidate`, ~L163) and `src/commands/create.ts` (`parentId`, ~L198).
- Keep `normalizeCliId()` unchanged so other id fields are unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `wl update <id> --parent null --json` sets `parentId: null`; `wl show <id> --json` confirms; no item is created or referenced as `WL-NULL`.
2. `wl create --title "x" --parent null --json` creates a top-level item (`parentId: null`).
3. `wl update <id> --parent ""` and `--parent none` both detach (documented aliases).
4. `wl update <id> --parent WL-DOESNOTEXIST` still errors (unchanged).
5. Unit tests for the new helper cover `null`, `NULL`, `none`, `-`, `""`, and a real/partial id.
6. CLI integration tests cover update-detach and create-top-level via `--parent null`.
7. `--parent` help text and `CLI.md`/`EXAMPLES.md` document detach.
8. `wl doctor` flags existing `WL-NULL` parent references; WL-0MLGTKNKF14R37IA and WL-0MLGTKO880HYPZ2R are cleaned to `parentId: null`.
9. `npm run build` and the full suite pass (build → test → commit order).

## Key files

- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `normalizeCliId`; add `normalizeParentId`
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--parent` handling (~L163)
- `src/commands/create.ts` — `--parent` handling (~L198)
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — dangling-parent check
- `tests/unit/cli-args.test.ts` (or equivalent) — helper unit tests
- `tests/cli/` — update/create integration tests
- `CLI.md`, `EXAMPLES.md`

## Notes

- Discovered during the ContextHub v1.0.16 release follow-up (WL-0MUJKVZTZ003FX8S); the same `--parent null` mistake was made while detaching the four hydrator follow-ups.
- `--parent null` for `wl list` / `wl search` (filter for root items) is a separate semantics question and is out of scope here.

# Pane-Triage Skill: Approval-Gated Idle Pane Cleanup

## Problem Statement

Agents that end with `</end_session>` leave their herdr pane open, causing idle panes to accumulate and hold memory/CPU. The automatic reaper (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3) handles unattended closure, but producers need a manual, workspace-scoped, approval-gated companion to review and close idle panes — particularly for panes with pending producer review or other special cases.

## Users

**Producer** — Runs several herdr workspaces with active agents. Wants to:
- *As a producer, I want `/skill:pane-triage` to scan my current workspace and report idle vs active panes, with work-item context and producer-review status, so I can decide which panes to close.*
- *As a producer, I want the skill to show a log tail for each idle pane, so I can verify completion before approving closure.*
- *As a producer, I want to explicitly approve or select which panes to close, so I retain full control.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:pane-triage` resolves the invoking workspace from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (fallback `herdr pane current`) and reports only that workspace.
2. Idle classification uses the **shared classifier** (`classifySession` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`) — the last non-empty session entry must be an assistant message ending with `</end_session>` (`.trimEnd()` then `endsWith('</end_session>')`).
3. The report renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle items, the work item id (parsed from pane label) and `needsProducerReview` value.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. A "Recommended to close" table lists idle panes and excludes the invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and panes with `needsProducerReview=true`; the never-close guard applies universally (manual and automatic).
6. No pane is closed without explicit producer approval (`yes`/`select`); `no`/ambiguity closes nothing; the invoking pane is never closed.
7. Approved panes are **re-verified** idle immediately before closing via re-read of `herdr pane list`; any pane that became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.
8. Offline fixture tests cover classification (via shared classifier), marker-mid-message rejection, work-item id parsing, `needsProducerReview` mapping, recommendation rules, and approval gating (no approval → zero close calls).

## Constraints

- **Shared classifier is mandatory** — do NOT reimplement idle state logic. Import `classifySession` and `extractFinalAssistantText` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`.
- **Shared reaper deps for closure** — import `createHerdrReaperDeps` and `runReaper` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` for pane enumeration and closure.
- **Never-close guards** (from classifier, universal): `implement` panes, items with `needsProducerReview=true`, the invoking pane, and panes with live child processes are never closed — **by both the automatic reaper and the manual skill** (producer confirmed).
- **Approval gate is mandatory** — this is the manual complement to the automatic reaper; it never closes anything unattended.
- **Workspace-scoped only** — no cross-workspace roll-up.
- **Skill placement**: Global skill at `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` (symlinked via `~/.pi/agent/skills/`). Tracked in ContextHub.

## Existing State

- **Shared classifier** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `classifySession()`, `extractFinalAssistantText()`, `DEFAULT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`, `SessionSample` type, `CloseDecision` type.
- **Reaper orchestration** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `runReaper(deps, options)`, `ReaperDeps` interface with `listPanes()`, `closePane(paneId)`, `terminateProcessGroup(pid)`.
- **Production wiring** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `createHerdrReaperDeps(io)`, `parseHerdrPaneCloseList()`, `paneKindFromLabel()`, `paneItemIdFromLabel()`, `readFinalAssistantEntries()`.
- **Dependency**: `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM → WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3` (completed, in_review).

## Desired Change

A new global skill `/skill:pane-triage` that:
1. Enumerates tabs and panes in the current workspace
2. Classifies each pane using the shared classifier
3. Enriches idle panes with work-item context and producer-review status
4. Displays a structured markdown report
5. Prompts for approval before closing
6. Re-verifies panes immediately before closing
7. Logs closure results in a per-pane ledger

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — Skill specification (what the agent reads)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/scripts/pane-triage.py` — Main skill script (invoked by agent)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py` — Python module with core logic:
  - `resolve_workspace()` — get workspace ID from env or `herdr pane current`
  - `enumerate_panes(workspace_id)` — call `herdr tab list` + `herdr pane list`
  - `classify_panes(panes)` — use shared classifier via `createHerdrReaperDeps`
  - `build_report(idle_panes, active_panes, invoking_pane_id)` — markdown output
  - `prompt_approval(recommended_panes)` — blocking prompt: yes/select/no
  - `close_panes(pane_ids)` — re-verify and close, one at a time
  - `parse_workspace_id()` — extract from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`
  - `get_needs_producer_review(item_id)` — call `wl show --json` to check
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/tests/test_pane_triage.py` — Offline fixture tests

## Related Work

- **WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3** — Implement closure reaper script (shared classifier, reaper orchestration, production wiring) — **COMPLETED**, dependency satisfied.
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — Log all dispatches and auto-close all completed dispatch panes (dispatch monitor) — completed.
- **WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN** — Implement auto-close logic with implement exception — completed.
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion — evaluated for deferral to this skill.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Should this skill live in the global skills directory or ContextHub-local? — A: **Global** at `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` (tracked in ContextHub), so it is available to all agents. ContextHub-local would limit availability.
- Q: How should a Python skill consume the TypeScript shared classifier? — A: **Producer (Q-OPEN-1):** Add a `--json` output mode to `runReaperCli` in ContextHub; the Python skill shells out to the compiled CLI. Keeps skill Python-only. Source: producer reply (intake).
- Q: May the manual skill close `needsProducerReview=true` panes after approval? — A: **Producer (Q-OPEN-2):** Never close — the never-close guard applies universally (manual skill + automatic reaper). Source: producer reply (intake).
- Q: How should the work-item id be parsed from the pane label? — A: Use the shared `paneItemIdFromLabel()` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — matches trailing ` - <PREFIX>-<HASH>` pattern.
- Q: Should `needsProducerReview` use the shared reaper deps or a direct `wl show` call? — A: Direct `wl show <id> --json` call in the skill script (the shared reaper deps' `getNeedsProducerReview` is for the reaper's injected I/O; the skill can call wl directly).
- Q: What is the exact idle classification check? — A: Use the shared `classifySession()` from `pane-close.ts` — it implements the `.trimEnd()` then `endsWith('</end_session>')` check. The skill must NOT re-implement this logic.
- Q: How should the skill handle herdr CLI errors? — A: Fail-closed: clear error message, no partial mutation. If `herdr pane list` fails, report the error and exit.
- Q: What happens if a pane becomes active during the approval prompt? — A: The re-verify-before-close step (AC7) handles this: re-read `herdr pane list` immediately before closing and drop any pane that is no longer idle.

## Open Questions (needs producer input)

### Q-OPEN-1 — How should a Python skill consume the TypeScript shared classifier?

**Context.** Skills in `SorraAgents/skill/` are Python-only (`~/.pi/agent/skills`
symlinks to `SorraAgents/skill`; no skill currently ships TypeScript/JS). The
mandated shared classifier, `classifySession` / `extractFinalAssistantText`, and
the reaper (`createHerdrReaperDeps` / `runReaper`) live in TypeScript at
`packages/herdr/src/pane-close*.ts` and compile to `packages/herdr/dist/`. There
is no standalone `herdr` CLI triage command and no `bin` entry, so there is no
current cross-language invocation path.

**Why it matters.** The spec says "import `classifySession` ... do not copy its
logic into the skill", but a Python module cannot import TypeScript. The choice
determines file layout, build/test story, and part of the effort estimate.

**Options.**

1. **Thin Node bridge (preferred).** Ship `scripts/pane-triage-bridge.mjs`
   which imports the compiled `dist/pane-close-herdr.js` + `pane-close.js`,
   enumerates panes, and emits a JSON report (classification + session tail) to
   stdout. The Python skill owns rendering, the approval prompt, re-verification
   and the ledger. Reuses the classifier verbatim; adds one non-Python script to
   a skill (unprecedented but small).
2. **Add a `--json` output mode to `runReaperCli`** in ContextHub and have the
   Python skill shell out to the compiled CLI. Keeps skill Python-only, but
   enlarges the shared surface (and the reaper is currently only wired into the
   herdr plugin, not exposed as a standalone binary).
3. **Write the skill in TypeScript/Node** under `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/`.
   Direct imports, but breaks the Python-skill convention and repo tooling.

**Preferred (needs confirmation):** Option 1.

### Q-OPEN-2 — May the manual skill close `needsProducerReview=true` panes after approval?

AC5 / the recommend-to-close rules say idle panes with
`needsProducerReview=true` **are** recommended to close, annotated
`review-pending`; the constraints say such items are "never closed". The
intended reading is that the never-close guard applies to the **unattended**
automatic reaper only, and the manual skill may close review-pending panes after
explicit producer approval. Confirm.

**Producer answer (Q-OPEN-2):** If marked `needsProducerReview`, do **not**
close. The never-close guard applies universally — to both the manual skill
and the automatic reaper. This resolves the AC5/approval conflict: `needsProducerReview=true`
panes are excluded from the "Recommended to close" table entirely.

# Intake Brief: Review Queue depth notification is incorrect

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only
`completed/in_review` count reaches `browseItemCount`. Today the banner copy is
fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.
- **Downtime dispatcher / operator** — must be unaffected: the banner is
  display-only and never gates dispatch (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the review queue is deep (root-only `completed/in_review` count ≥
   `browseItemCount`) **and** at least one root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Review queue deep (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`.
2. When the review queue is deep **and** no root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
3. "Outstanding audit" is determined by the existing audit-freshness semantics
   (`isAuditFresh` / `inReviewBucket`): an `in_review` item with no stored
   `auditedAt`, or whose stored audit is not current, counts as outstanding. A
   fresh, passed audit does not.
4. The banner remains display-only: it never disables downtime dispatch, never
   writes/clears `.herdr-downtime-disabled`, and does not change code-freeze
   banner behaviour or the `showHelpText` gate.
5. Automated tests assert the exact rendered banner text for both variants and
   for the boundaries (deep+outstanding → deep+none; deep → shallow), using the
   existing worklist render test seams.
6. All related documentation/code comments describing the banner are updated to
   the new copy and the outstanding-audit condition.

## Constraints

- **Source repository:** the banner is implemented in the **ContextHub** repo
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`). This work item is tracked in the
  ContextHub worklog after migration from AI_Hell (`AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ`);
  implementation targets the ContextHub source tree.
- `browseItemCount` default 20, re-read live from settings (no restart).
- Root-only counting via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` (same query as `fetchCompletedItemCount`).
- No new persistence mechanism; reuse existing fetch helpers where possible.
- Display-only; must not reintroduce the sprint-complete auto-disable
  (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD RCA root cause A).
- Keep the change minimal: banner copy + the state needed to choose it.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` renders the banner in the footer branch
  (~3596–3617): `const bannerText = \`Review queue deep${countDisplay} — audits will drain it\`;`
  where `countDisplay` = ` (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review)`.
- `refreshSprintState()` (~4531–4546) calls `fetchCompletedItemCount()`
  (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ~684) and sets
  `sprintComplete = count >= liveBrowseCount`. Only a count is retained —
  per-item audit state is not currently available to the banner.
- `fetchCompletedItemCount()` runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` and returns the item count. `wl list --json` items expose
  `stage`, `status`, `auditedAt`, `auditResult`, `fingerprint`, `updatedAt`
  (but not `currentFingerprint`).
- Audit freshness is centralised: `isAuditFresh(...)` in
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (~306) and the audit-aware bucket predicate
  `inReviewBucket(...)` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (~360–389). The
  audit-dispatch tier uses the same predicate.
- There are currently **no automated tests** covering the banner text or
  `refreshSprintState` — this gap must be closed.

## Desired change

- Extend the banner-state refresh (or add a sibling helper) so it knows whether
  any root-level `in_review` item has an outstanding audit, in addition to the
  deep-queue boolean.
- Select the banner copy from that state:
  - outstanding audits → `Review queue deep (<n> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`;
  - none outstanding → `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
- Add regression tests for both variants and the transition boundaries.
- Update the code comments that describe the banner to match the new copy and
  condition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — banner copy selection in the footer render
  branch (~3596–3617); `refreshSprintState` (~4531–4546); render-option plumbing
  for `sprintComplete` / `sprintCompletedCount` (~3359–3396, ~5893–5894).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchCompletedItemCount` (~681–699): extend
  or replace with an outstanding-audit-aware fetch of root `completed/in_review`

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only

fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.
- **Downtime dispatcher / operator** — must be unaffected: the banner is
  display-only and never gates dispatch (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD).

   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.

   `auditedAt`, or whose stored audit is not current, counts as outstanding. A

   existing worklist render test seams.
